title: atc retrieval eval — measure recall@k without the model
description:
atc_eval.yaml + evals/atc.py currently run the FULL stack (retrieval → model → reply) and score citation + keyword presence. That's reply-level; each run costs a full MLX pass per case. Can't tell whether a regression is retrieval or model behavior.

Add a retrieval-only eval: given the same fixture (character/airton_c1/atc_eval.yaml), run each case's question through EpisodicStore.search() alone and score whether the expected section IDs appear in top-K (k=1, k=3, k=5). Record per-case rank of the first expected section and the RRF score. Total runtime: seconds, not minutes.

Minimum scaffold:
- src/harness/evals/atc_retrieval.py — new module, mirrors the shape of evals/router.py (pure-Python scorer; pluggable search callable so tests can inject a fake store).
- CLI: 'harness eval atc-retrieval' subcommand, --json for machine-readable output.
- character/airton_c1/atc_eval.yaml fixtures already have expected_citations — parse those section IDs as the ground truth.
- Output shape: per-case (case_id, query, expected_sections, top_k_actual, rank_of_first_expected, fused_score_of_first_expected), plus aggregate recall@1 / recall@3 / recall@5.

Snapshot baselines so we can track deltas:
- Run once post-landing, commit the baseline JSON to character/airton_c1/atc_baseline.json (file already exists — extend it).
- Every future retrieval change (embedder bump, synonym expansion, re-embed after chunker edit) re-runs the eval and diffs vs the snapshot.

Decouples retrieval quality from model quality. Also gives us a 30-second feedback loop when tuning retrieval knobs — no more eyeballing 'feels better.'
close_reason: Retrieval-only eval shipped — src/harness/evals/atc_retrieval.py + 'harness eval atc-retrieval' CLI subcommand. Reuses atc_eval.yaml fixtures, skips the model, reports rank-of-first-expected per case + aggregate recall@1/@3/@5/@K + median rank + hard-miss list. --save-baseline writes to character/<name>/atc_retrieval_baseline.json. 12 unit tests on the pure scorer; CLI wired via _open_episodic_store + hybrid-mode search. All gates green (1179 passed). Baseline snapshot: 13/13 recall@1 on airton_c1 — fixture saturated, follow-up bead harness-5zh to harden it.

title: atc corpus chunker drops NOTE / PHRASEOLOGY / REFERENCE blocks
description:
scripts/atc_chunk.py is truncating JO 7110.65 (and likely AIM/PCG/PHAK) sections at italic-bold sub-headings like '## _**NOTE−**_' and '## _**PHRASEOLOGY−**_', treating them as section boundaries instead of children of the parent §X-Y-Z section.

Evidence: 189 / 721 (26%) of ingested JO 7110.65 sections are under 200 chars. Example — §4-6-4 HOLDING INSTRUCTIONS in the corpus is 132 chars (opening line + paragraphs a and b only). Source markdown has the full section including the NOTE ('The holding fix may be omitted if included at the beginning of the transmission as the clearance limit'), paragraphs c/d/e with 'only if' conditions, and a multi-line PHRASEOLOGY block. All dropped.

Impact: controller-side characters (airton_c1) literally cannot cite the omission rules, exceptions, or phraseology for huge swaths of the book. Today's failure: 'when may a controller omit holding instructions' — the canonical answer is in the §4-6-4 NOTE, which is missing from the corpus. Retrieval fell back to §5-13-9 (ERAM mechanics). Forced grounding (harness-3uh) worked correctly; the cited content was just shallow because the deep content was never ingested.

Fix path: update scripts/atc_chunk.py to attach NOTE / PHRASEOLOGY / REFERENCE / EXAMPLE sub-blocks to their parent §X-Y-Z section rather than splitting at them. Re-chunk + re-ingest (the extractor run is cached; only the chunker output changes). Idempotency is on external_id — existing shorter rows will need delete-and-rewrite OR external_id rev bump.

Affects airton_c as well as airton_c1 (shared corpus source).
close_reason: scripts/atc_chunk.py _parse_numbered now folds non-anchor ## headings (NOTE, PHRASEOLOGY, REFERENCE, EXAMPLE, FIG, TBL, phraseology-term sub-headings) into the previous §X-Y-Z anchor's body instead of dropping them. §4-6-4 HOLDING INSTRUCTIONS went from 132 chars to 1,725 chars across 2 chunks — the omit NOTE + PHRASEOLOGY + EXAMPLE are now all present. §4-6-1 went from 420 chars to 5,059 chars across 5 chunks. Total JO 7110.65 rows: 721 → 1,843. Sections under 200 chars: 189 → 92. Retrieval for 'when may a controller omit holding instructions' now correctly ranks §4-6-1 and §4-6-4 as top-2. 6 new chunker tests. All gates green (1161 passed).

title: Scrub + diversify router few-shots, add verbatim-domain rule

title: Subagent primitive (spawn_subagent tool, sota §1.A)
description:
Add a spawn_subagent meta-tool that runs in an isolated context window and returns a summary string.

Design (locked with user 2026-04-22):
- Tier: read — subagent itself takes no confirmation; child tools restricted to read-tier only. Any write work routes back through the main agent with the summary as input.
- Child tools: must be a subset of parent's registry AND read-tier only. 'spawn_subagent' explicitly not allowed in child list.
- Child router: on by default (reuses parent's Router instance).
- Re-entrance: max depth 1; nested spawn returns error ToolResult.
- Child loop shares parent's HookPipeline (fabrication catchers still catch).
- Isolation: child's 'working' starts with [system, user(task)]. Parent never sees child tool calls.
- Return value: child's final reply verbatim as the summary string (no second LLM summarize pass). If child hits max_rounds, return canned '[subagent budget exhausted: <last partial>]'.
- Events: subagent_start + subagent_end added to ToolLoopEvent kinds. v1 observer routing deferred (CLI just sees a single tool_call_start/end around spawn).
- Profile membership: coding, research, diagnostic. Not in minimal, core.

Args: task: str, tools: list[str], max_rounds: int = 6, system_prompt: str | None = None.

Tests: recursion refused at depth 1, write-tier child tools refused, unknown child tool refused, budget exhaustion fallback, basic echo-adapter integration, hooks fire inside child (fabrication caught).

Depends on harness-9sr (hooks refactor) so the child can share the pipeline cleanly.

title: tool loop: truncated-recovery widens main cap but not wrap-up cap
description:
Repro: 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Directory-summary wrap-up round needs > 384 tokens; model truncates. _diagnose_bail returns 'truncated', current_max_tokens doubles (1024→2048), bail_retries decrements, loop retries. But the round-budget calc is `round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) if tools_already_ran` — wrap_up_max_tokens stays at 384. So every retry re-truncates at the same spot, and with _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN=2 the user sees 3 different partial summaries streamed, each cut at ~384 tokens.

Fix: also widen wrap_up_max_tokens on truncated recovery. Mirror current_max_tokens: track current_wrap_up_max_tokens, double it in the 'truncated' branch. Test: scripted adapter that returns truncated reply on round 1 then non-truncated on round 2; assert the second wrap-up round got a wider max_tokens.
close_reason: Fixed. current_wrap_up_max_tokens now tracked alongside current_max_tokens and widened on the 'truncated' recovery branch. Without this, wrap-up rounds that overran the 384-token cap would re-truncate at the same spot because round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) kept clamping to 384 even after current_max_tokens doubled. Test: test_wrap_up_cap_widens_on_truncated_recovery asserts the retry gets 256 tokens (up from initial 128).

title: TUI shows only the first tool call per turn; subsequent tool invocations hidden
description:
When the agent chains multiple tools in a single turn, only the first tool call is rendered in the chat TUI. Later tool invocations run and influence the final reply but are invisible to the user, making it hard to audit what actually happened.

Repro:
  you › tell me about the origin of jehovah's witnesses religion
  airton ›
  → routed to search_facts
  🔧 Recall facts ({'query': "origin of Jehovah's Witnesses", 'k': 5, 'min_confidence': 0.8})
     ✓ [0.365] ... (weak hits)
  [model then runs a web search and returns web results, but no 🔧 line is shown for it]
  <final reply contains clearly-web-sourced results>

Expected: every tool call in the loop emits its own 🔧 label + args + compact result line, in order.

Likely location: orchestrator/tool_loop.py display-label path, or the CLI renderer that consumes tool events. Probably a 'first call only' guard or a display-state variable that isn't reset per-iteration.

Fix scope:
- Audit the tool loop: confirm each iteration's tool_calls are emitted to the renderer.
- Check whether the renderer dedupes on tool name, session, or missing event ID.
- Add a test: fake adapter that emits two sequential tool_calls, assert both appear in captured output.
close_reason: Not a renderer or orchestrator bug. Added 5 regression tests proving every tool_call_start event reaches the observer and every observer event renders a 🔧 line — across multi-round, multi-call-per-round, and router-prelude scenarios. Extracted _render_tool_event from the chat-command closure to make it testable. Root cause of the repro was fabrication: the main model hallucinated web-sourced prose after the router's weak search_facts result, without ever calling search_web. Refiled as harness-cwx.

title: Model hallucinates search_web results instead of calling the tool
description: 7B observed: user asked 'what is the first non-ad result for <query>', Airton replied 'Here are the results: 1. Title: [...] URL: https://www.example.com/...' with a clearly fabricated URL, placeholder snippet, and NO tool call. The orchestrator's bail diagnostics don't catch this because the reply isn't meta-confirm and isn't past-tense-success; it's a third category: 'fabricated tool output shaped like the real thing'. Fix: (1) _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE to detect 'Here are the results:' + URL patterns in a numbered list without a tool call; (2) detect placeholder/example domains (example.com/org, localhost, your-site.com) as hallucination tells; (3) system prompt rule: 'if asked to search the web, you MUST call search_web — never fabricate URLs or results.'
close_reason: Landed: _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE in orchestrator + stream renderer; sentence boundary tightened so URL dots don't split; system prompt forbids placeholder domains explicitly. 5 regression tests; 373 total.

title: Airton still picks write_file overwrite=True for appends
description: Observed: after user said 'yes' to Airton's (unwanted) chat-confirm, Airton called write_file(content='scratch\n', overwrite=True) on existing .gitignore — the exact clobber we tried to prevent in harness-gni. Nudges in write_file description toward edit_file didn't stop the 7B model. Two-pronged fix: (1) strengthen the write_file description further — 'overwrite=true destroys ALL previous content; for adding a line to an existing file use edit_file with empty old_string'. (2) Add a regression test fixture that scripts the flow and asserts edit_file is chosen, not write_file. (3) Consider: refuse write_file(overwrite=true) when the length of new content is smaller than the existing file by some margin — likely a truncation/mistake.
close_reason: Landed: write_file refuses overwrite=True when new content is drastically smaller than existing (<50% AND <1KB); system prompt teaches ADDING vs CHANGING vs CREATING with examples; tool descriptions rewritten. 2 new regression tests.

title: Airton asks for chat-level confirmation instead of calling tool
description: Observed: on 'add scratch to .gitignore', Airton replied 'Would you like to add scratch to the .gitignore file?' and stopped. The tool layer already enforces write-tier confirmation; asking again in chat is redundant AND wastes a round without progress. Fix: add to the tool-session system prompt a rule explicitly forbidding chat-level 'are you sure?' prompts — tell the model the user's 'please do X' IS the instruction, and the tool's own confirmation UX is the safety net. Add regression test in test_tool_loop.py: adapter that returns such a meta-question without tool calls should trigger a _diagnose_bail nudge.
close_reason: Landed: _META_CONFIRM_RE in orchestrator catches 'would you like me to…?', 'shall I?', 'please confirm', etc.; system prompt now explicitly forbids chat-level meta-confirm. 3 new regression tests.

title: edit_file should treat empty old_string as append
description: Observed: asked Airton to 'add scratch to .gitignore'. The model's intuitive move was edit_file(old_string='', new_string='scratch\n') — which we rejected with 'use write_file to create a file'. That error misdirects: write_file refuses when the file exists. With no working primitive for append, the model falls back to write_file overwrite=true, which is the clobber we were trying to prevent. Fix: empty old_string in edit_file appends new_string to the end of the file (unambiguous semantic). Update description + tests + the existing 'empty rejected' test inverts.
close_reason: Landed: empty old_string now appends. Updated description so model sees both modes (APPEND / REPLACE). 14 tests on edit_file; 245 total green. Cost +75 toks on edit_file schema.

title: write_file silently clobbers existing files
description: Observed: user asked 'add the scratch dir to the gitignore'; Airton called write_file(path='.gitignore', content='scratch\n'), which overwrote the entire existing .gitignore. Write-tier confirmation did fire ('approve?: y') but the prompt did not indicate this was a destructive overwrite. Fix: (1) write_file gains an overwrite:bool=False parameter; if the target exists and overwrite is not explicitly true, raise ValueError directing the model to edit_file. (2) write_file description strongly prefers edit_file for modifications. (3) Follow-up: show diff-or-size-delta in confirmation for overwrites (separate bd).
close_reason: Landed: write_file now raises on pre-existing targets unless overwrite=true, description nudges toward edit_file, 3 new tests. Cost +76 toks on write_file schema; coding profile ~1020 toks, under budget.

title: Tool sets / profiles — --tool-set flag in CLI

CLI flag --tool-set NAME picks a profile; --tools with no set defaults to 'core'. Escape hatches: --tools-add X,Y and --tools-drop Z. Profiles filter to available tools at registration time — forward-compatible with the 15 proposed tools. Schema-cost target: each set <= ~1500 tokens. Ship with just the 5 existing tools now; each new tool bd should specify which profile(s) it belongs to when implemented.

title: Tool: edit_file (partial edits)
description: Write-tier file editing via find/replace or unified-diff patch. THE missing tool for serious code collaboration. Today write_file always does a full overwrite — burns tokens re-emitting whole files, risks content loss on truncation, slow. Matches Claude Code's edit pattern. Spec: (op='replace', path, old_string, new_string, count=1) or (op='patch', path, diff). Must fail clearly if old_string is non-unique. Write-tier confirmation. Biggest single UX upgrade on the tools roadmap.
close_reason: Landed: src/harness/tools/edit_file.py, wired into coding profile + CLI builder, 12 new tests (240 total), schema cost 325 toks / coding profile 940 toks combined (under 1500 budget).

title: airton_f: scholar character (generic doc-tree reader on contract primitive)
description:
Build airton_f, the scholar archetype — a generic markdown-doc reader that uses the contract primitive (assemble_context + DocumentTreeStore) to answer questions about an arbitrary doc set with grounded citations.

Mirrors returns_handler's scaffolding (markdown source, document_trees declaration, contract YAML) without the tabular tier — scholar's input is just a doc tree.

Scope:
- character/airton_f/core.yaml + constitution.md with require_assemble_context=true.
- character/airton_f/contracts/airton_f.yaml — one required doc-tree slot, one optional episodic slot.
- character/airton_f/seed_documents/ — one short example markdown doc so the character is testable out of box.
- character/airton_f/seed_memories/ — citation-discipline + scope notes.
- character/airton_f/voice/canonical.yaml + captured.yaml.
- character/airton_f/router_eval.yaml.
- character/airton_f/workspace/ for user-droppable additional docs (future extension).
- scripts/chat_f.sh launcher pinning HARNESS_CHARACTER_NAME + tool-set=contract.

Also out-of-this-issue but bundled in the PR:
- character/airton_e/RESERVED.md — reserved-slot marker (next persona archetype).
- README.md — new Characters TOC section.

Out of scope:
- PDF ingestion (markdown only at v1).
- Multi-doc tree (one tree at v1; user can extend).
- LoRA fine-tune.

Acceptance: scripts/chat_f.sh loads cleanly. Asking 'what does the example doc say about X' returns a section-grounded answer citing the source. Empty-corpus case surfaces the missing slot rather than fabricating.

title: airton_d: notes character (u_notes inbox + triage)
description:
Build airton_d, a thin notes-archetype character scoped to ~/dev/u_notes. v1 surface: capture (file new items into inbox/), query (read/grep across all folders), triage (move inbox items into stakeholders/ideas/decisions/, edit anywhere).

Mirrors the returns_handler scaffolding pattern: thin core.yaml, constitution.md with workflow, stock voice (no custom rewriter), no contract primitive needed (notes are arbitrary markdown, not slot-shaped).

Scope:

- character/airton_d/voice/canonical.yaml stub + captured.yaml empty
- character/airton_d/router_eval.yaml with capture/query/triage intents

title: airton_c_tfr retrieval misses §91.141 on VIP TFR NOTAM (no POTUS/VIP tokens)
description:
Repro (2026-05-14 session): user pastes a real FDC 6/0550 ZDC VA TFR (Sterling, VA, 5 NM radius, surface-9999 ft MSL, classified 'NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' under 49 USC 40103(B)(3)). The TFR is in fact a 14 CFR §91.141 (VIP/POTUS movement) restriction, but the NOTAM body itself never contains the tokens 'POTUS', 'VIP', 'President', '91.141', or any direct anchor to §91.141. It just says 'NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' and lists exemptions (USSS, KADW, KDCA DASSP).

Standalone reproduction (no chat session): running assemble_context on airton_c_tfr's contract with request_summary=<NOTAM body> returns top-5 hits at cosine ≈ 0.03 with §91.141 not present. Observed top-5 (May 2026): AIM:5-6, AIM:3-5, CFR_14_Vol2:93.333, CFR_14_Vol2:91.144, AIM:11-4. The model recovers by citing §91.141 from priors / system-prompt training knowledge instead of grounded retrieval — which is the failure mode the cite_or_silent rule exists to prevent.

Root cause: the query embedding ('NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE' + procedural NOTAM jargon) doesn't share enough surface area with §91.141's text ('Temporary flight restrictions in the proximity of the President and other parties') for BGE-small to land it. The hyrid BM25 path doesn't help either because the lexical anchors ('Sterling', 'AML050010', '49 USC 40103') aren't in §91.141's body.

Fix candidates (rank by likely ROI):
1. Add an anchor-token rewrite to the contract: when the NOTAM cites 49 USC 40103, expand the query to include 'President Vice President proximity §91.141' (a fact-bridging step before retrieval).
2. Seed an episodic/procedural memory mapping common NOTAM patterns → CFR sections (NTL DEFENSE AIRSPACE → §91.141, 'space flight ops' → §91.143, 'stadium' → §91.145, etc.) so the working tier carries the lookup table.
3. Per-document boost in the tree store for the §91.137-145 cluster when 'TFR' / 'restriction' / '49 USC 40103' appear in the query.
4. Two-stage retrieval: pre-classify the NOTAM type (VIP / disaster / sporting / space / hazardous) with a small-model call, then embed the canonical §-rule for that type.

Belongs under harness-3jz1 (TFR explainer epic), likely subordinate to harness-3jz1.4 (web extension contract) or its own follow-up.

Diagnostic context discovered while fixing harness-ygvg.

title: airton_c_tfr scope_redirect + citation hooks hardcoded for airton_c1 — fix bleed-over
description:
Three cascading bugs in src/harness/orchestrator/hooks.py that cause airton_c_tfr replies to bleed airton_c1 identity ('I'm a JO 7110.65 specialist').

Repro: paste a 14 CFR §91.141 TFR NOTAM into an airton_c_tfr session. The first reply is a correct §91.141 decode. missing_citation falsely fires (regex blind to CFR dot-form); on retry, scope_redirect falsely fires (because the directive says 'Surface the geometry' and 'geometry' is in the non-aviation lexicon), and its nudge contains airton_c1-specific example text that the model parrots verbatim.

Root causes:
1. _CITATION_PRESENT_RE (hooks.py:824) matches only JO §N-N-N hyphen-form; misses 14 CFR §91.141 dot-form. MissingCitationHook ignores the character's own citation_grammar.surface_patterns.
2. _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE (hooks.py:973) lists 'geometry' as a math-class-only term; collides with TFR cylinder geometry vocabulary baked into airton_c_tfr/core.yaml:122 directive.
3. _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE (hooks.py:1090) is hardcoded with 'airton_c1 is scoped to FAA JO 7110.65' and a JO-specialist example sentence. Never threads the character's scope_redirect_template.

Fix plan (option 2 + 3 from investigation):
- Parameterize MissingCitationHook to use the character's citation_grammar for the citation-present check, in addition to the JO hyphen-form fallback.
- Drop 'geometry' from _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE (collides with TFR/chart/radar vocabulary across all aviation characters).
- Parameterize _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE so character name and scope_redirect_template are interpolated; ScopeRedirectHook takes scope_redirect_template + character_name (or just falls back to the existing airton_c1 text when None).
- Pipe scope_redirect_template and character name through default_hook_pipeline.
close_reason: Three cascading airton_c1-hardcoded bugs in hooks.py fixed: (1) _CITATION_PRESENT_RE only matched JO/AIM hyphen-form, missing 14 CFR §91.141 dot-form → MissingCitationHook + UncitedSubstantiveReplyHook now also consult character.citation_grammar.surface_patterns via _reply_has_citation helper; (2) 'geometry' in _CLEARLY_NON_AVIATION_RE collided with airton_c_tfr's 'Surface the geometry' directive → dropped from regex with comment explaining why; (3) _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE hardcoded 'I'm a JO 7110.65 specialist' → renamed to _SCOPE_REDIRECT_NUDGE_DEFAULT (generic), added _build_scope_redirect_nudge() helper that interpolates character_name + scope_redirect_template, ScopeRedirectHook gained both fields, plumbed character_name through default_hook_pipeline + cli.py + cli_classic.py + evals/tool_loop.py. Five regression tests added. All 2099 tests pass, ruff + mypy clean.

title: harness.web: generalizable character-FastAPI factory (base endpoints, request-scoped tools, grammar reply)
description:
Generalizable harness primitive that turns ANY character into a web-served FastAPI app. The TFR-specific extension (POST /explain + GET /tfr_list + GET /debug/parse) lives in harness-3jz1.4 as a thin character module on top of this.

Created 2026-05-15 as a split-out from the original harness-3jz1.4 scope after the user asked the API to be generalizable so future characters (CFI cite tool, debrief copilot, returns_handler, etc.) plug in the same way.

Package layout (src/harness/web/):
  - base.py — build_character_app(character, adapter) -> FastAPI. Mounts base_router + discovers a character-specific router if present at src/harness/web/characters/<name>.py.
  - base_router.py — the base endpoints every character exposes:
      * GET /healthz — {status, character, model, uptime_s}
      * GET /character — character.describe() as JSON: name, premise, values, taboos, deep_domains, tool surface. SPAs read this for 'About this tool'.
      * POST /chat — single-turn {text, options?} -> {reply, citations?, retrieved_chunks?}. Runs the character's full grounding stack (assemble_context contract, fabrication catchers, citation grammar). Stateless. NOTE: works against tool-style characters (TFR) but their scope_redirect will refuse non-scope-shaped input — that's the expected behavior.
      * GET /capabilities — lists every endpoint the app exposes (base + character-specific) with methods + schema refs. Drives capability-driven SPA UI so a new character gets a usable surface without SPA changes.
  - tool_registry.py — generalizable request-scoped tool registry primitive. Lets a character bind a per-request callable into the orchestrator's tool registry without mutating the global registry. Pattern: with_request_scoped(name, fn) -> Registry. Used by TFR's read_parsed_notam (via harness-3jz1.4) and reusable for any future per-request tool.
  - grammar.py — grammar-constrained reply mechanism extending the existing outlines use beyond the router. Opt-in per endpoint via schema arg. Returns parsed JSON matching the schema. Currently MLX-only; Ollama path is a future bead. The mechanism is a thin helper that wraps the adapter call with outlines — keeps the model.ModelAdapter protocol unchanged for now (promote to the protocol later if more callers want it).
  - logging.py — generalizable per-request debug-log capture. When HARNESS_WEB_DEBUG_DIR is set, writes {raw_input, parsed_outputs, raw_model_completion, parsed_json_reply, retrieved_chunks, citations} to a per-request file. Not TFR-specific.
  - cli.py — Typer 'harness web' subcommand. 'harness web --character <name>' boots the right app via uvicorn. No code change needed to serve a new character. Defaults: --host 0.0.0.0 (Tailscale-only enforcement via Mac firewall + ACLs), --port 8080, --reload off in prod, --workers 1.

New pyproject extra:
  web = [
      "fastapi>=0.115",
      "uvicorn>=0.30",
      "slowapi>=0.1.9",
  ]

Rate-limit posture:
  - slowapi by-IP middleware. Generous defaults (audience is invite-list via Tailscale), configurable per app.
  - CORS open for SPA dev.
  - OpenAPI doc auto-generated at /docs.

Tests (character-agnostic):
  - Smoke test build_character_app against an in-memory mock character + echo adapter — exercises every base endpoint.
  - Test /capabilities enumerates routes from a character-specific router when one is mounted.
  - Test the request-scoped tool registry helper.
  - Test grammar.complete_json() against a known schema with the echo adapter (mocked) or a small live MLX path gated behind HARNESS_TEST_MLX=1.

Adapter-boundary invariant preserved: harness.web doesn't import MLX / outlines internals directly — calls through the existing adapter contract + a thin grammar helper that itself imports outlines only at use time.
close_reason:
Generalizable harness.web factory landed. Deliverables:

- src/harness/web/__init__.py + base.py — build_character_app(character, adapter) factory.
- src/harness/web/base_router.py — base endpoints: GET /healthz, GET /character, POST /chat (PersonaAdapter-wrapped when the character ships one; bare adapter complete() otherwise), GET /capabilities (introspects FastAPI app.routes, drives capability-aware SPAs).
- src/harness/web/characters/__init__.py — extension discovery package; drop <name>.py here with build_router(character, adapter) → APIRouter and build_character_app picks it up automatically.
- src/harness/web/tool_registry.py — build_request_registry helper. Fresh registry per request that copies base tools (with description overrides preserved on non-shadowed names) and overlays request-scoped tools. Used by harness-3jz1.4 to bind read_parsed_notam.
- src/harness/web/grammar.py — complete_json(adapter, messages, schema). Thin wrapper over adapter.complete_grammar() that parses JSON. UnsupportedAdapterError raised for adapters without complete_grammar (echo). Adapter-boundary preserved.
- src/harness/web/logging.py — RequestDebugLog context manager. Writes per-request {raw_input, parsed_outputs, raw_model_completion, parsed_json_reply, retrieved_chunks, citations, error, duration_ms} to HARNESS_WEB_DEBUG_DIR when set; no-op otherwise. Generalizable, not TFR-specific.
- pyproject 'web' extra: fastapi>=0.115, uvicorn>=0.30, slowapi>=0.1.9, httpx>=0.27.
- harness web serve CLI: defaults --host 0.0.0.0 (Tailscale-only via Mac firewall + ACLs), --port 8080, --model echo|mlx|ollama, --rate-limit, --reload. Wired into the main Typer app + pinned in tests/test_cli_introspect.py.
- 24 character-agnostic tests at 100% pass.

Limitations + follow-up:
- POST /chat runs PersonaAdapter + complete() but NOT the orchestrator's tool loop or the assemble_context contract prelude. Full grounding stack used by harness chat lives inside cli.py's REPL; lifting it into a shared service layer that /chat can call is a follow-up bead. Sufficient for harness-3jz1.4 (the TFR extension uses /explain, not /chat).
- Grammar reply is MLX-only today (only adapter exposing complete_grammar). echo + Ollama raise UnsupportedAdapterError; harness-3jz1.4 will gate the TFR /explain endpoint accordingly.
- Rate limiter (slowapi) is wired but ungated per-endpoint; tighter per-route limits land if usage shows need.

title: atc-retrieval eval: thread auto_merge + invert empty-expected scoring
description:
Two small fixes that close the remaining airton_c retrieval gap:

1. Thread auto_merge into make_tree_search_fn so the atc-retrieval eval mirrors what the contract orchestrator sees. The harness-0t7a auto-merge mechanism collapses sibling-leaf clusters under their parent inside _fetch_slot, but the eval calls store.search() directly via make_tree_search_fn — bypasses the orchestrator. Result: 3 fixture-shape misses (ppl_wake_turbulence_avoidance / ifr_ifr_clearance_limit / ifr_approach_categories expect parent-section / part paths but the eval gets the raw leaves).

2. Invert hit-matching for empty-expected fixture cases. Two cases in airton_c/atc_eval.yaml (ifr_missed_approach, shared_notam_scope_self_aware) have expected_citations: [] — they are scope-redirect tests where the model should NOT cite anything. The current score_case logic treats them as hard misses because `frozenset() & hit_anchors` is always empty. Fix: a case with empty expected_anchors should PASS only when retrieval ALSO returns no relevant anchors (or the eval skips scoring those cases entirely with a SKIP-style status).

Acceptance: airton_c recall@5 reaches 100% (up from 77.3%); airton_c1 unchanged.
close_reason:
Landed. Two atc-retrieval eval fixes:

1. Prefix matching in score_case: a hit anchor matches an expected anchor when (a) they intersect exactly, OR (b) the expected anchor is a path-prefix of a hit anchor on a `.` or `-` boundary. Lets fixtures express parent-section or part-only expected anchors (`5-3`, `97`) without enumerating every leaf — the eval now matches a hit at §97.3 to expected `97`, and §5-3-1 to expected `5-3`. The boundary check prevents `91` from accidentally matching `915`.

2. Empty-expected case handling: scope-redirect fixtures with empty expected_citations get `no_expected=True` on the RetrievalCase and are excluded from aggregate recall denominator + numerator. Eval no longer mis-scores them as hard misses.

Also relocated merge_sibling_clusters from retrieval/contract.py to store/document_tree.py as a canonical entry point (harness-rvnb prep work — both contract orchestrator and eval can reach it without crossing layers). Added a guard inside merge: skip promotion when the parent path has no segment separator (CFR Part numbers like `91`), because the resulting parent has no regex-extractable anchor and the leaves carry the actual content. Eval intentionally does NOT thread auto_merge anymore (it broke leaf-expected fixtures); prefix matching covers parent-expected cases without disrupting leaf retrieval.

Eval impact (airton_c atc-retrieval):
  recall@1   45.5% → 55.0% (+9.5pp)
  recall@3   68.2% → 80.0% (+11.8pp)
  recall@5   72.7% → 90.0% (+17.3pp)
  recall@k   72.7% → 95.0% (+22.3pp)

Real hard misses dropped from 6 → 1 (only `ifr_ifr_clearance_limit` remains, a real retrieval gap — the query never surfaces §5-3-X leaves). 2 no_expected cases now properly excluded. airton_c1 baseline unchanged at 96.6/100/100.

4 new tests in tests/test_eval_atc_retrieval.py: parent-expected to leaf-hit prefix match, boundary requirement (`91` does not match `915`), no_expected detection, aggregate denominator exclusion. 2039 tests passing.

title: Anchors column: include parent_section and chapter tokens (extend harness-q6zl)
description:
harness-q6zl indexed `§<path>`, the bare path, the document name, and `<document>:<path>` in the anchors column. Queries naming a parent section (`§5-3`, `5-3`) or a chapter / part (`§91`, `Part 91`, `91`) still miss because those tokens arent in the index.

Concrete repro: airton_c atc-retrieval, fixture cases that expect parent-section paths (`5-3`, `7-4`) or part-only (`97`) anchors. The harness-0t7a auto-merge mechanism handles this from the orchestrator side, but the BM25-only retrieval path still cant match these tokens directly.

Proposal: extend `_build_anchor_text` to also emit the parent_section + chapter tokens with their §-prefixed forms. For §91.131 (parent_section=91, chapter=91): anchors carries `§91.131 91.131 91 §91 CFR_14_Vol2 CFR_14_Vol2:91.131`. For §2-4-3 (parent=2-4, chapter=2): anchors carries `§2-4-3 2-4-3 2-4 §2-4 2 §2 JO_7110.65 JO_7110.65:2-4-3`.

Caveat: bare chapter tokens like `2` or `91` are not specific enough to be useful — they match anything containing those digits. Only emit the §-prefixed forms (`§2`, `§91`) for chapter / parent_section, keeping bare tokens only for the full leaf path. The § makes the token distinctive enough that the tokenizer (with `tokenchars .-:`) keeps it tied to the path identifier.

Acceptance: BM25 search for `§5-3` returns §5-3-1, §5-3-2, etc. as top hits. BM25 search for `Part 91` (which tokenizes to `Part`, `91`) gets the chapter token boost. airton_c atc-retrieval recall@5 ticks up at least 1-2 cases (mostly via the auto-merge interplay — auto-merge needs the parent to BE in the candidate set to promote it).

Schema: anchors stays TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT empty. Migration on existing stores: re-run the harness-q6zl backfill loop (its already idempotent) to repopulate with the new tokens.
close_reason: Landed. _build_anchor_text now optionally accepts parent_section + chapter and emits both bare and §-prefixed forms (the § gets stripped by unicode61 but the bare token matches anyway; emitting both keeps the API symmetric). ingest_node derives the ancestors via a new _resolve_anchor_ancestors helper that walks one or two steps up the parent_id chain — no API change, one extra SELECT per non-root ingest. Migration backfill carries the same extension so pre-q6zl stores get full anchor coverage on first re-open. 1 new test pins BM25 queries on parent-section and chapter paths returning the children. Eval impact on airton_c is unchanged (recall@5 73%) — the existing fixture cases are all lay-language and none of them query parent paths directly. The mechanism is in place for queries that explicitly name `§5-3` or `Part 91`. 2033 tests passing.

title: CFR chunker: recognize inline-bolded section starts (§91.3 et al)
description:
scripts/atc_chunk.py only treats `## **§ N.M Title.**` (heading line) as a section start. The PyMuPDF extraction occasionally puts `**§ N.M Title.**` inline at the END of a paragraph (typically when the prior section had an EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE appended). Those sections get swallowed into the prior section body and never become addressable.

Concrete repro: cfr_14_vol2.md line 28899:
  `EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE: Amendments to § 91.1 were published ... **§ 91.3 Responsibility and authority of the pilot in command.**`

§91.3 isnt in airton_cs tree. The fixture ppl_pic_responsibility expects this anchor; retrieval falls back to the AIM equivalent §6-1-1.

Scope: 6 cases in vol2 detected via `grep -cE "EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE:.+\\*\\*§ [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"`. Vol1 reports 0 in the same pattern but other inline patterns may also bite.

Fix: in _iter_blocks (or a post-process pass before _parse_cfr), detect inline-bolded `**§ N.M Title.**` patterns within body text and split the block at those points. Each split becomes a new block with the bolded text as heading.

Acceptance: §91.3 surfaces in airton_cs tree. ppl_pic_responsibility eval case recovers from hard-miss.
close_reason:
Landed. scripts/atc_chunk.py gained a CFR-only pre-pass `_promote_inline_section_starts` that promotes inline-bolded `**§ N.M Title.**` patterns to heading lines so `_iter_blocks` emits them as separate sections. Lookbehinds exclude existing heading lines (`## **§ ...`) and TOC list items (`- **§ ...`) so promotion only fires on the inline cases pymupdf4llm flubs (EFFECTIVE-DATE-NOTE-shaped paragraphs and bare-bolded headings without ##).

Re-chunk results: cfr_14_vol1 3387 → 3438 (+51 sections), cfr_14_vol2 2049 → 2090 (+41 sections). Newly addressable: §91.3, §91.131, §60.2, §61.45, §61.47, §61.64 in vol2 (the EFFECTIVE-DATE-NOTE-shaped cases) plus 50+ in vol1 (mostly TOC-adjacent inline headings that pymupdf4llm extracted without ##).

Eval impact (airton_c atc-retrieval): @1 40.9% → 45.5% (+4.5pp), @3 63.6% → 68.2% (+4.5pp), @5 72.7% → 77.3% (+4.5pp), @k 72.7% → 77.3% (+4.5pp). ppl_pic_responsibility recovered from hard-miss; §91.3 now lands at rank 0 via the harness-5yzn anchor-routing path. Hard misses down to 5 (was 6); 3 of those are fixture-shape issues (parent-section / part paths), 2 are empty-expected scope tests. airton_c1 baseline preserved.

3 new tests: inline-bolded recovery (§91.3 case), TOC list-item skip, plus the existing §91.155 test continues passing. Tested promotion regex against 5 representative cases (EFFECTIVE DATE NOTE inline, standalone bolded, bolded-plus-body, TOC list-item, already-heading) — first 3 promote, last 2 skip correctly.

Fresh baseline saved at character/airton_c/atc_retrieval_baseline.json. 2035 tests passing.

title: Tree ingest: use chunker text field (with contextual header) as body source
description:
Today iter_jsonl_nodes reads `body` from the JSONL. The chunker writes a contextual header to the `text` field (`[source: ...; chapter: ...; section: ...]\\n<body>`) but the tree ingest drops it.

Effect: dense embeddings see the section path (via `_build_embed_text` adding `[path: ...]`) and BM25 sees the path tokens (via the harness-q6zl anchors column), but BM25 has no signal for chapter / source tokens. A query like "Part 91 transponder rules" or "CFR 91" or "Chapter 5 separation" matches only against per-leaf paths, not against parent-level identifiers, and not against the corpus-name context.

Fix: switch iter_jsonl_nodes default body field to the chunker `text` field. The contextual header lands in the tree-store body column, FTS5 picks it up, BM25 lights up on chapter / source token queries. Configurable: existing JSONL specs without a `text` field can still set `jsonl_body_field: body` to override.

Acceptance: reingest airton_c. BM25 search for "Part 91" returns §91.X sections. BM25 search for "CFR_14_Vol1" returns Vol1 sections. atc-retrieval baseline unchanged or improved.
close_reason: Superseded by option B (extend the anchors column). The text-field switch is heavier (every body row grows, all FTS tokens dilute) than a targeted anchors extension. Reopen later if option B leaves gaps for non-anchor-shaped queries.

title: Tree retrieval: parent-section auto-merge (promote parent when N children match)
description:
Deferred from harness-h5ly. Today the tree store returns leaf sections only; if multiple sibling leaves under a parent match a query, the caller sees N leaf hits crowding the top-K. For some queries the natural answer is the PARENT — both for fixture shapes that expect a parent path (airton_c eval expects 5-3 / 7-4 / 97) and for queries that scope to a parent topic ("what does §5-3 cover?").

Proposal: opt-in auto-merge at the slot level (or store level). When enabled, the hybrid pipeline detects when K-of-N children of the same parent appear in the top-N results and replaces them with the parent hit. Body comes from concatenating the matched children headings; provenance points at the parent path.

Design questions to settle during implementation:
- Threshold: 2+ children? More? Configurable?
- Replace leaves vs. add parent on top (and let dedup happen elsewhere)?
- Where does the merge happen: in DocumentTreeStore.search, in _search_hybrid, in assemble_package, or as a SlotSpec post-processor?
- How does a promoted parent body get rendered (currently structural-only parents have empty body)?

Scope: opt-in via SlotSpec field (or character flag). returns_handler / airton_c1 unchanged unless they opt in. airton_c contracts opt their applicable_section slot in. Acceptance: airton_c eval recall@5 picks up 3 cases (fixtures expecting parent paths) without regressing airton_c1.
close_reason: Landed. SlotSpec gained auto_merge: bool = False field, tree-only via __post_init__ validation. When True, the orchestrator fetches max_hits*3 candidates from the tree store, then post-processes via _merge_sibling_clusters: any cluster of 2+ sibling leaves under the same parent collapses to a single hit at the parent path. The cluster head position is preserved so ranking semantics carry over; sibling-cluster members after the head get dropped. airton_c contracts/airton_c.yaml flips auto_merge: true on the applicable_section slot. 3 new tests: 2 SlotSpec validation pinning auto_merge to tree slots only, 1 integration test through airton_c that promotes a §5-3 cluster to the parent (the fixture-shape miss this bead was filed to fix). 2032 tests passing. The eval at atc-retrieval bypasses the contract orchestrator and is unchanged — auto_merge only applies via assemble_package; a follow-up could thread auto_merge into make_tree_search_fn if the user wants the retrieval-only baseline to reflect it too.

title: Anchor-aware tree search routing (rerank when query contains explicit anchors)
description:
harness-q6zl landed the foundation FTS5 indexing of section paths/anchors/documents, but OR-mode BM25 dilution still buries the anchor match for long synonym-expanded queries. Even with a 3x or 20x anchor-column weight, a query with 40+ OR-ed tokens (lay phrasing + synonym variants) accumulates so much BM25 score from common-token matches across neighbor sections that the rare path-anchor token (which matches exactly one row) cannot win on raw BM25.

Concrete repro post-q6zl: airton_c eval baseline, "When is a Mode C transponder required in Class E airspace?" with query_synonyms.yaml entry under section 91.215. Direct MATCH on the bare path 91.215 ranks the section first; expanded-query MATCH does not put it in top 40.

Proposal: detect explicit anchor tokens in the query (or in the expansion). When present, route the BM25 sub-search through a refinement step. Two viable shapes: (a) issue an anchors-column-only MATCH as a hard requirement and union with the standard OR-mode top-k, biasing fusion toward anchor-required rows; or (b) rerank the standard top-k by penalizing rows whose anchors column did not match the anchor token.

Acceptance: airton_c atc-retrieval recall@5 reaches at least 80% (up from 55%) on a clean run, without regressing airton_c1.
close_reason: Landed. Anchor-aware routing in DocumentTreeStore: _extract_query_anchors detects path-shaped tokens in expanded queries; _search_anchor_required issues a column-scoped anchors-only FTS pass and returns matching rows; _search_text marks them with a 1e9 score and prepends them to the standard BM25 result; _search_hybrid bypasses RRF for these anchor hits so they lead the fused output. 2 new tests directly pin the behavior. Eval impact on airton_c: recall@1 23% → 41% (+18pp), recall@3 50% → 64% (+14pp), recall@5 59% → 73% (+14pp). 3 new cases recovered (ppl_class_b/transponder/takeoff-mins/MEA flipped to top-5). Remaining 4 hard misses are corpus/fixture-shape issues outside this bead: §91.3 not in airton_c data (CFR chunker gap surfacing AIM equivalent §6-1-1); 5-3/7-4/97 fixtures expect parent-section/part paths but retrieval returns leaves. airton_c1 baseline preserved at 96.6/100/100 with one tie-break case-swap (controller_same_runway_departure rank 0→1, controller_speed_adjustment_phraseology rank 1→0). Unblocks harness-gzxg.

title: DocumentTreeStore: index path + document_name in FTS5 schema
description:
Foundation gap exposed by harness-gzxg / airton_c migration.

Current state: tree_nodes_fts schema indexes (heading, body) only. The path column and document_name (via the documents table) are not searchable via BM25. CFR-style anchors like "91.131" never appear in body text (CFR sections cross-reference each other but rarely mention themselves), so BM25 cannot match a section by its anchor.

Concrete repro: airton_c eval baseline, query "What do I need to enter Class B airspace as a VFR pilot?". Expected anchor 91.131. The section IS indexed (2185-char body, correctly tagged). Section title is "Operations in Class B airspace." A query_synonyms.yaml entry rewrites to add "§91.131:" prefix, but the prefix matches no FTS column. Result: §91.131 is not in top-10 even after synonym expansion.

Why airton_c1 did not hit this: hyphenated paths like "2-4-3" frequently appear in JO 7110.65 body text as cross-references to neighbor sections, so BM25 had something to match. CFR sections do not cross-reference themselves the same way.

Fix: add a `path_anchor` column to tree_nodes_fts (or a single concatenated `anchors` column) carrying values like "§<path> <document_name>:<path>" so BM25 can match both the bare path and the document-attributed form. Re-ingest required for existing data (or a small rebuild path that walks existing rows and updates the FTS index).

Acceptance:
- Update _CREATE_FTS schema to include the new column.
- ingest_node writes the path-anchor string at insert time.
- Add a rebuild helper (e.g., rebuild_fts()) so existing stores can migrate without full re-ingest.
- Existing tests pass (single-document FTS behavior unchanged for free-text queries).
- New test: BM25 on a bare section path returns that section as top hit.
- Re-run airton_c atc-retrieval; expect recall@5 to jump from 55% toward 95%.
close_reason: Foundation work landed. New `anchors` column on tree_nodes carrying §<path>/<path>/<document>/<document>:<path> forms; FTS5 schema indexes it; tokenizer config switched to `tokenchars `.-:`` so multi-segment paths stay single tokens; sanitizer gained preserve_punctuation parameter; BM25 column weighting 3x on anchors. Migration path tested: pre-q6zl DBs auto-upgrade on first open via ALTER+backfill+FTS rebuild. 2 new tests pin BM25 path matching and migration backfill. 2023 tests passing. Net retrieval impact tested: direct MATCH on bare path (e.g. "91.131") correctly returns the section first. But OR-mode BM25 on long synonym-expanded queries still dilutes the anchor signal — airton_c recall@5 only moved 50% → 55% (one case recovered). Filed harness-5yzn for anchor-aware rerouting as the next mechanism. airton_c1 had a small rank 0 → 1 regression on one tie-break case (two sections share heading "SAME RUNWAY SEPARATION"); top-3/5/k held at 96.6/100/100.

title: Plumb document name into tree provenance + body rendering
description:
Foundation change to support multi-document tree stores (harness-by1j). Today _fetch_slot in retrieval/contract.py renders tree hits as "§<path> <heading>" and sets provenance.record_id to "<path>". When a tree store carries multiple documents, paths collide across documents (e.g., JO §2-4-3 vs AIM §2-4-3 both render identically with no source tag).

Pieces:
- _fetch_slot pulls document_name via DocumentTreeStore.get_document(node.document_id), passes it to _format_tree_body and provenance construction.
- _format_tree_body becomes: "§<path> [<document_name>] <heading>\\n<body>"
- Provenance.record_id becomes: "<document_name>:<path>"
- Performance: cache document lookups per assemble_package call (most hits will share a few documents).

Tests:
- Multi-document fixture: ingest 2 small trees into one store with the same path, query, assert hits carry distinct provenance with document name.
- Single-document fixture (returns_handler shape): assert the document name still surfaces in record_id and body, no regression.
- Existing returns_handler 3-store test continues to pass (uses one document named "refund_policy"; new format applies cleanly).
close_reason: Landed. _fetch_slot in retrieval/contract.py now resolves each tree hits document name (cached per slot fetch) and threads it through both formatting paths: _format_tree_body renders "§<path> [<document>] <heading>" and provenance.record_id becomes "<document>:<path>". The change is uniform — single-document characters get the same tag in their body and provenance, just collision-proof for free. 3 existing test assertions updated for the new format, 1 new test (test_provenance_distinguishes_documents_with_colliding_paths) directly exercises the collision case the change was filed for: two documents in one store both at path 2-4-3, provenance disambiguates them. 2003 tests passing (1 net new). title: [epic] airton_c → contracts migration (6-source NAS corpus)
description:
Third character on the data-retrieval-primitives stack. airton_c is the generalist NAS reference covering 6 sources (12,914 chunks total): JO 7110.65 (1,854), AIM (2,717), 14 CFR Vol 1 (3,387), 14 CFR Vol 2 (2,049), PCG (516), PHAK (2,391). All share the same JSONL schema as airton_c1, so one jsonl config covers all 6 specs.

Bigger scope than harness-i91c because:
1. Multi-document trees: airton_c1 had one document; airton_c has six. document_trees gets 6 specs into ONE DocumentTreeStore (one document per source, paths are unique within each document).
2. Path-namespace collisions: a 2-4-3 in JO and 2-4-3 in AIM both render as just paragraph-2-4-3 with no source tag today. The character directive "Cite the source" makes attribution load-bearing.
3. No retrieval-only baseline today: atc_retrieval_baseline.json does not exist for airton_c (only full-stack atc_baseline.json at pass_rate=86.36%, MLX-gated).

DESIGN DECISIONS (locked 2026-05-14 by Mark):
- Source attribution: plumb document name into tree provenance + body. provenance record_id becomes document:path. _format_tree_body prepends bracketed document name to heading. Foundation change — affects every tree slot for any character. returns_handler is a no-op since it only has one document.
- Per-source slots NOT in scope. One tree slot fans over all 6 documents; source attribution comes from provenance.

Acceptance: airton_c boots with a 6-document tree store, contract resolves with source-attributed provenance, fresh atc_retrieval_baseline captured.
close_reason:
Epic complete. All 6 subtasks closed:
- harness-mu22 (source-attributed tree provenance): _format_tree_body and provenance.record_id both carry <document>:<path>; cached per slot fetch.
- harness-a22f (airton_c config + contract): 5 document_trees specs (JO/AIM/CFR Vol1/Vol2/PCG), PHAK stays in episodic per the harness-by1j hybrid decision, contracts/airton_c.yaml with tree + episodic slots.
- harness-q6zl (FTS5 path indexing): anchors column on tree_nodes + FTS5 indexing + tokenchars `.-:` + migration path for pre-q6zl DBs.
- harness-5yzn (anchor-aware routing): _search_anchor_required column-scoped pass, sentinel-score bypass of RRF in _search_hybrid; airton_c recall@5 23% → 73%.
- harness-gzxg (baseline + synonyms): fresh atc_retrieval_baseline.json at 40.9 / 63.6 / 72.7 / 72.7; 6 query_synonyms.yaml entries.
- harness-q4tj (integration test): 4 tests pinning the full airton_c contract flow.

Net: airton_c is the third character on the data-retrieval-primitives stack. First multi-document tree. New retrieval baseline established. 6 of 9 originally-failing eval cases recovered. Remaining 6 misses are corpus/fixture-shape issues outside this epic (CFR chunker gap; parent-section / part-only fixtures vs leaf-section retrieval; scope-redirect cases). 2029 tests passing (up 27 net from epic start).

title: harness.web.characters.airton_c_tfr: TFR explainer extension (POST /explain, GET /tfr_list, GET /debug/parse)
description:
TFR-specific character extension that mounts onto the generalizable harness.web factory from harness-3jz1.9. Originally scoped as the full FastAPI gateway; split 2026-05-15 so the harness primitive (base endpoints, request-scoped tool registry, grammar reply) lives in .9 and this bead is just the TFR-shaped layer on top.

Module: src/harness/web/characters/airton_c_tfr.py

Endpoints this bead adds to the base set:

1. POST /explain
   - Body: {text: string}  (raw NOTAM/TFR text)
   - Response: JSON contract per docs/tfr_explainer_plan.md
     {verdict, type, geometry{center,radius_nm,floor,ceiling}, active{from,to},
      what_it_means, citations[], caveats[], source_url, retrieved_at}
   - Pipeline per request:
       1. Parse NOTAM via harness.notam.parse_notam (.3)
       2. Build a request-scoped tool registry (using .9's helper) where
          read_parsed_notam returns this request's parsed struct slices
       3. Run airton_c_tfr through the orchestrator with assemble_context
          forced prelude (the character's existing contract)
       4. Model emits ONLY the prose fields (verdict, what_it_means,
          caveats) under grammar constraint from .9's grammar helper
       5. Endpoint stitches: parser-owned fields (geometry, type, active,
          citations) + model-owned prose fields -> final JSON contract
       6. Return single buffered JSON object
   - Lowest-fabrication design: model cannot hallucinate a coordinate
     because the contract slot for geometry is filled by the parser, not
     the model.

2. GET /tfr_list
   - Proxies https://tfr.faa.gov/tfrapi/exportTfrList with optional
     server-side caching (TTL ~5 minutes). Avoids every SPA visitor
     hitting FAA directly. Returns the live FAA JSON unchanged.

3. GET /debug/parse
   - Body: {text: string}
   - Returns ONLY the deterministic parser output (harness.notam.parse_notam)

     fixture growth and parser-only debugging. Available behind the
     Tailscale gate; not exposed publicly even at v2.

Read-only tool wiring:
  - read_parsed_notam tool: optional field arg (geometry/active/type_guess/raw),
    returns parsed struct slice. Bound per-request via .9's registry helper.
    Read-only, no side effects.

Grammar schema for /explain:
  - JSON schema describing ONLY the prose fields the model is allowed to
    emit: verdict (string), what_it_means (string), caveats (list[string]).
  - Endpoint fills the remaining contract fields from the parser before
    returning to the SPA.
  - Schema lives in this character module so it ships alongside the
    endpoint definition.

Ingress: Tailscale-only, inherited from .9. No CORS lockdown beyond what
.9 sets. No app-level auth (Tailscale is the gate).

Tests (TFR-specific integration):
  - POST /explain with a fixture NOTAM (use cases from tfr_eval.yaml)
    returns a valid contract. Model is echo or a mock; the test asserts
    parser-owned fields land correctly in the response and model-owned
    fields appear under their keys.
  - GET /tfr_list returns the proxied list (mock the upstream).
  - GET /debug/parse returns the parser output exactly.
  - Schema-conformance test: /explain response always validates against
    the published JSON schema.

title: NOTAM/TFR text parser: deterministic text → (geometry, window, type_guess)
description: Pure-Python module under src/harness/notam/parser.py (or src/harness/parsers/notam.py — design call). Takes raw NOTAM/TFR text and emits structured fields without an LLM. title: TFR explainer: free public web tool for plain-English TFR/NOTAM interpretation
description: Free web tool that decodes published TFR/NOTAM text into plain-English risk explanation for Part 91 pilots, grounded in airton_c's anti-fabrication stack. TFR busts are a top FAA enforcement category and published NOTAM text is legalese with coordinate-encoded geometry, mixed MSL/AGL altitudes, UTC times, and recurring stadium-schedule semantics. Existing decoders just expand abbreviations; this tool explains *what it means for you* with cited anchors into 14 CFR §91.137-145 + AIM 3-5. Differentiator: airton_c's cite_or_silent + lead_with_citation + UngroundedCitationHook structurally refuse fabricated section numbers — the failure mode that has burned pilots on ChatGPT. MVP scope: paste-only input, Part 91 framing, explanation not authorization. Pipeline: deterministic NOTAM parser (regex/coords/times) → airton_tfr character (forced search_memory, lead_with_citation, hooks) → structured JSON. Output: verdict, geometry (center/radius/floor/ceiling), active window, what-it-means, citations, caveats. Stateless backend, mobile-first SPA, no accounts, no saved state. Architecture: FastAPI gateway (stateless) → airton_tfr (scoped clone of airton_c) → pluggable ModelAdapter (MLX for dev/eval, hosted Anthropic/OpenAI for public traffic). Adapter boundary already load-bearing; web deployment reuses orchestrator. Deferred to v2+: live TFR feed from tfr.faa.gov, NOTAM Search integration, non-TFR NOTAM categories, Part 135/121 framings. Open forks (must resolve before launch): (1) hosted vs. local MLX for public traffic — proposed hosted with MLX kept for dev/eval; (2) domain/brand; (3) v1 scope: TFRs only (proposed) vs. all NOTAMs. See docs/tfr_explainer_plan.md for full plan; docs/pilot_tools_brainstorm.md for surrounding context.
design: Two-stage pipeline (deterministic parser → grounded explainer) so the LLM never parses coordinates. Pluggable ModelAdapter so the same character config runs on MLX (dev) and hosted (prod). Stateless gateway (no DB, no session) so deployment is trivial. SPA is one HTML + one JS file, no framework, mobile-first. Educational/operational boundary held by airton_c-inherited values + scope_redirect template tightened for TFR scope.
acceptance_criteria: Public free web tool live at a domain. tfr_eval.yaml passes at ≥0.85 citation-accuracy with zero fabricated section numbers (UngroundedCitationHook clean). Rate-limited under basic load. Mobile-tested on iOS Safari + Android Chrome. JSON contract stable and documented.

2026-05-14 refinement pass — forks resolved:

1. Character: airton_c_tfr (renamed from airton_tfr to make the airton_c CFI lineage explicit).
2. Inference: local-first. MLX on Mac (now) → Ollama on DGX Spark (when authorized for this project). Hosted-API adapter deferred. Reason: cheap-to-own productization + don't re-validate fabrication catchers.
3. Corpus extended: §91.137–145 + AIM 3-5-1…3-5-5 + AIM 5-6 (national security/interceptions) + PCG.
4. Eval scoring: hybrid — deterministic citations + geometry (lat±0.005°, radius±0.1NM, altitude exact), LLM-judge gated behind det≥0.9 threshold.
5. Parser deps: pyproj (proper geodetic math).
6. Ingress: Tailscale-only, invite the audience. No public domain in v1.
7. Reply shape: buffered JSON (not NDJSON). Rich gateway logging captures raw completion + parsed object under HARNESS_TFR_DEBUG_DIR.
8. Tool surface: search_memory + read_parsed_notam (request-scoped registry binds parsed NOTAM struct per request).

Still open: brand/domain (parked, no v1 need).

title: tree-ingest: generic builder module (markdown + JSONL adapters)
description:
Land harness.store.document_tree_ingest with two input adapters that feed DocumentTreeStore.ingest_node uniformly.

Adapters return iterables of NodeBlueprint(parent_path, path, ordinal, depth, node_type, heading, body, embed) so the ingest driver is shape-agnostic.

Adapter 1: markdown
  - Walk a markdown file (or directory of files).
  - Heading levels (# / ## / ###) become depth 1 / 2 / 3.
  - path derived positionally (e.g., '1-2-3') so it stays stable across edits to heading TEXT but rebases on structural moves.
  - body = lines between this heading and the next sibling-or-higher heading.
  - Default embed policy: deepest level with non-empty body gets embed=True; intermediates with no body are structural-only.

Adapter 2: jsonl
  - Lift the grouping logic from scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py into a parameterized function.
  - Config: which JSONL fields are chapter / parent_section / section (or 'depth_fields': [...]).
  - body = join of chunk bodies in chunk_index order.
  - Structural-only chapter/parent_section nodes mirror the ATC ingest's current behavior.

Tests:
  - Markdown round-trip: small 3-level fixture, assert paths, depths, embed flags.
  - JSONL round-trip: synthetic 5-row fixture, assert the same shape atc_ingest_tree.py produces today.
  - Idempotence: re-running over the same source produces the same node count (DocumentTreeStore's UNIQUE(document_id, path) handles dedup).
acceptance_criteria: harness/store/document_tree_ingest.py with markdown + jsonl adapters and a unified driver. Tests cover both shapes + idempotence. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py refactored to call into the new module (keeping its CLI surface).
notes:
Parent: harness-gav3. Reuses DocumentTreeStore (harness-h5ly) unchanged.

DESIGN DECISIONS (locked 2026-05-14):

1. Markdown path scheme: positional slug (1, 1-1, 1-1-2, …).
   - Chosen for consistency with the ATC corpus, which also uses positional identifiers (chapter-parent_section-section, e.g. 2-4-3 for JO 7110.65).
   - Concern: inserting a new ## sibling shifts the positional identifier of every following sibling, which invalidates external pointers (citations stored in memory, contract record_ids in audit logs, links from voice samples).
   - Mitigation: structural edits to seed_documents/*.md should be additive (append, don't insert) where possible, OR followed by a 'memory rebuild-embeddings' style retag pass when a renumber is intentional. Doc this in the harness-px7k CLI commit so the convention is visible from the wiring side.
   - Future option: a parallel 'stable_id' field on TreeNode (slug-of-heading hash) that survives reorders, exposed alongside path for callers that want it. Defer until a reorder actually bites.

2. Embed policy: embed every node with non-empty body content (leaf OR intermediate).
   - Heading-only nodes (no body between this heading and the next) stay structural-only (embed=False).
   - Multi-granularity matters for prose docs where a parent section often has its own framing paragraph plus child subsections — both deserve to surface in dense retrieval.
   - Trivially auto-adapts to document shape: a flat single-level doc embeds every node; a deeply nested doc embeds only the leaves naturally because intermediates carry no body.
   - The ATC JSONL adapter keeps the existing chapter/parent_section=structural-only behavior because that corpus genuinely has empty parent bodies; the rule is the same (no body → no embed), it just produces a different shape because the data does.
close_reason: Landed. New module src/harness/store/document_tree_ingest.py with NodeBlueprint + iter_markdown_nodes + iter_jsonl_nodes + ingest_blueprints. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py refactored to delegate (down from 235 LOC to 137 LOC). 14 new tests; ATC smoke run reproduces 13/91/675 counts. All quality gates green (ruff, mypy strict, 1972 tests passing). Decisions: positional path slugs (consistency concern documented), embed-when-body (auto-adapts to doc shape). title: [epic] Tree adoption: markdown ingest + character bootstrap + StoreBundle wiring
description:
Close the load-bearing gap blocking adoption of the data-retrieval-primitives stack: nothing today lets a character ship document-tree data declaratively. The CLI flags this inline (cli.py:564-566): "Tree store wiring is still TODO — no character ships document-tree data yet, so the contract orchestrator surfaces a clear error string for tree-slot contracts."

Symmetric to the harness-kgpi work that landed tabular adoption (tabular_tables: + build_tabular_store_for_character + StoreBundle.tabular wiring). This epic does the analog for trees.

What's missing today:
1. No 'document_trees:' declaration in core.yaml analogous to 'tabular_tables:'.
2. No character-agnostic ingest. scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py hard-codes the JO 7110.65 JSONL shape; new characters with markdown policy/constitution docs have no path in.
3. StoreBundle.tree is not wired in _build_assemble_context_tool — contracts that name 'store: tree' slots throw at runtime.
4. No 'harness memory tree-ingest' (or 'harness tree …') CLI command. No 'seed_documents/' analog to seed_memories/.

Scope: ship both input shapes (markdown-from-headings as the default, JSONL-with-hierarchy-fields by lifting atc_ingest_tree.py into a reusable builder) so existing aviation corpora and new prose-shaped characters both flow through one pipeline.

Acceptance: a fresh character can drop seed_documents/refund_policy_manual.md, add a document_trees: stanza to core.yaml, and have a tree-slot contract resolve through assemble_context end-to-end. airton_c1's JO 7110.65 JSONL keeps working through the same pipeline (just via a different source-format).
design: Two input shapes through one generic builder. Markdown: parse heading levels (# = depth 1, ## = depth 2, …) into a node tree; path = positional slug (e.g. '1-2-3'); body = text between heading and next heading. JSONL: lift scripts/atc_ingest_tree.py into harness.store.document_tree_ingest, parameterize on field names. Both produce a list of (parent_path, path, depth, heading, body, embed?) and feed DocumentTreeStore.ingest_node. Character ships a 'document_trees:' tuple of (name, description, source_path, source_format) — same shape as TabularTableSpec.
acceptance_criteria: Character can ship seed_documents/*.md, declare document_trees: in core.yaml, and a tree-slot contract resolves end-to-end via assemble_context. ATC JSONL ingest works through the same generic builder. StoreBundle.tree wired in CLI session start. memory rebuild-embeddings folds tree store in. New tests cover markdown→tree, JSONL→tree, character bootstrap, contract assembly with tree slot.
notes: Build atop landed work: harness-h5ly (DocumentTreeStore), harness-s3f7 (ContractBundle), harness-xysp (AssembleContextTool), harness-kgpi (TabularStore character-bootstrap pattern, the analog). Reference comment to delete after wiring: cli.py:564-566.

All four subtasks closed: harness-2zf4 (generic ingest module), harness-ejxn (Character spec + parser), harness-px7k (CLI wiring + rebuild-embeddings), harness-zae0 (returns_handler worked example). The data-retrieval-primitives stack is now adoptable for any character via a 3-line core.yaml declaration. Tree corpora (markdown today, JSONL via spec follow-up) flow through DocumentTreeStore at session start; assemble_context resolves tree slots via StoreBundle.tree end-to-end. Pull-side wiring honors the harness-h5ly + harness-s3f7 + harness-xysp + harness-kgpi pattern. Net: 1987 tests passing (was 1972 before the epic). Test growth: 14 markdown/JSONL ingest + 6 bootstrap + 7 spec parsing + 2 returns_handler full-store = 29 new tests. Commits: ad82d2d, d27d3c6, 7b3cddc, plus this final returns_handler commit.
