title: atc-5: section-aware chunker → episodic JSONL
description:
Section-aware chunker that turns extracted markdown into retrieval-ready rows. Input: character/airton_c/corpus/markdown/*.md. Output: character/airton_c/corpus/chunks/<doc_slug>.jsonl (one row per addressable section or merged-sibling block).

Row shape (ingest target for EpisodicStore tier='seed', user_id=NULL):
{
  'source': 'JO_7110.65BB' | 'AIM' | 'PCG' | 'PHAK' | 'CFR_14_61' | 'CFR_14_91',
  'chapter': '2',
  'section': '2-6-4',
  'title': 'ISSUING WEATHER AND CHAFF AREAS',
  'text': '...paragraph text with the section anchor embedded for retrieval fidelity...',
  'parent_section': '2-6',
  'principle': '<mapped to airton_c taxonomy>'
}

Parsing per source:
- JO 7110.65 / AIM: section anchors are N-N-N (e.g., 2-6-4). Parse markdown heading trail.
- PCG: term-per-entry, use term as 'section', empty 'chapter'.
- CFR Title 14: Part → Subpart → § §N.NNN. Use § number as section.
- PHAK: chapter-based; section is chapter/sub-heading.

Size target: aim for 400-1200 char chunks (retrieval sweet spot). Merge short sibling blocks under the same section; split long ones on paragraph boundaries with an 80-char overlap for continuity.

Contextual chunking header (matches existing episodic embed-text convention): '[source: JO_7110.65BB; chapter: 2; section: 2-6-4]\n<body>'.

Acceptance: sample 10 rows and verify each has a well-formed anchor, and the body contains readable text (not Unicode-escaped nonsense, no page-number noise).

Depends on atc-4. Blocks atc-6.
notes:
Chunker shipped; Phase-1 corpus chunked to JSONL. IMPLEMENTATION: - scripts/atc_chunk.py (~570 LOC) — heading-stack walker + per-source parsers + size shaper. Four parser kinds: 'numbered' (AIM/JO 7110.65), 'cfr' (CFR Title 14 §N.M), 'glossary' (PCG), 'phak'. Pure function chunk_markdown(md, cfg) → list[Chunk]. - Contextual header per row: [source: X; chapter: Y; section: Z]\n. ASCII hyphen in section anchors (normalised from U+2212 in source). - Size shaper splits > 1200 char bodies on paragraph boundaries with 80-char overlap, indexed via chunk_index. Short bodies pass through. - Page-noise filter: dates (2/20/25), solo section numbers, short doc-name footers (AIM/PCG/Pilot's Handbook/14 CFR Ch.), orphan page numbers. - Argparse CLI: --only SLUG, --force, --input, --output, --sample N, --seed S. TESTS (17 new, all green): - _iter_blocks segmentation - _strip_wrappers (markdown emphasis) - _clean_body (noise drop + blank collapse) - _parse_numbered: unicode-minus normalisation, explanation-prefix stripping, chapter tracking, empty-body skip - _parse_cfr: §N.M capture - _parse_glossary: letter-as-chapter, frontmatter skip (PURPOSE / EXPLANATION OF CHANGES) - _split_oversized: pass-through, paragraph-split with overlap - _expand_by_size: chunk_index indexing - Chunk.text contextual header (full + minimal) - write_jsonl roundtrip pyproject: ruff per-file-ignores for RUF001/002/003 on atc_chunk + test_atc_chunk — U+2212 in regex + docstring is the point. OUTPUT (character/airton_c/corpus/chunks/, gitignored): pcg.jsonl — 516 rows aim.jsonl — 802 rows jo_7110_65.jsonl — 738 rows phak.jsonl — 2,391 rows cfr_14_vol1.jsonl — 3,350 rows cfr_14_vol2.jsonl — 2,037 rows Total: 9,834 rows. ACCEPTANCE — sampled 10 random rows (--seed 42): - Anchors well-formed: CFR (25.331, 5-4-8, 45.11, 33.72, 25.1153, 23.2600, 21.41), AIM (5-4-8), JO 7110.65 sections via spot-check (1-1-1, 2-6-4, 5-4-10). - Bodies readable; no page-header / date / solo-section-number noise reached the chunks. - ASCII hyphens throughout; U+2212 successfully normalised in metadata (original bodies preserve source chars, which is fine for keyword retrieval). KNOWN PHASE-1 GAPS (not blocking; file as follow-ups when retrieval signals demand): - PCG: pymupdf4llm doesn't emit a ## heading per glossary term — some terms (AAM, ABEAM, ABORT, etc.) land in the body of a sibling term's chunk. Bodies still contain the individual definitions so keyword-BM25 hits; only the 'section' metadata is less precise. - JO 7110.65 / AIM: each doc ships with an 'Explanation of Changes' block that re-states every touched anchor's section number. Results in duplicate section IDs across chunks (change-description row + real-content row). Downstream ingest can dedup by (section, body_hash) if necessary. - PHAK: unnumbered subheadings → parser falls back to chapter-level granularity. Some
HTML artifacts leak through for list-heavy chapters. Quality gates: ruff clean, mypy strict (165 files), pytest 1074 passed / 3 env-gated skips. BLOCKS unblocked: atc-6 (ingest) and atc-7 (eval).
close_reason: Section-aware chunker shipped; 9,834 chunks across 6 docs with normalised anchors, contextual headers, and page-noise filtering. 17 new tests green (1074 total). Known PCG / change-block / PHAK gaps noted for atc-6 dedup or retrieval tuning as signals demand.

title: Self-introspection: agent can describe its own abilities, tools, commands, and limits
description:
Give the agent first-class awareness of its own capabilities so it can answer 'what can you do?', 'what tools do you have?', 'what's your context window?', 'who are you connected to?' accurately instead of hallucinating.

Scope:
- Abilities: currently-loaded tool set (resolved from profile + add/drop), per-tool name + one-line purpose + write-tier flag.
- Model surface: adapter backend (mlx/ollama/echo), model repo, LoRA path if any, context window, tokens used / remaining this session.
- Memory surface: episodic + semantic counts, last consolidation time, seeded memories count, current embedder id + dim.
- Character surface: character name, loaded personae, voice sample count (canonical + captured).
- CLI commands: the same reference that lives in CLAUDE.md / docs/usage.md, but sourced from the Typer app itself so it can't drift.
- Limits/taboos: what it will refuse, what it can't do yet (e.g. no web unless web tool loaded).

Implementation sketch:
- A read-only 'introspect' tool (or set of tools: introspect_tools, introspect_memory, introspect_model, introspect_commands) the agent can call when asked.
- Alternative/additive: a rendered capability block the orchestrator can inject into the system prompt on demand (token-cheap, but staler and always-on).
- Prefer the tool route: keeps the default system prompt lean, the agent only pulls it when the user asks.

Touches: tools/ (new tools + register in profiles), orchestrator/tool_loop.py (no changes if tools follow the existing protocol), character system prompt (maybe a single line: 'If asked what you can do, call introspect_*').

Ties in with harness-7ee (router debug) — introspection could surface router state too.

title: tool loop: short-circuit duplicate tool calls within a turn
description:
Repro: prompt 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Model emits summary prose + list_dir({'path': '', 'recursive': true, 'include_hidden': false}) in the same reply. The orchestrator records the prose as assistant history and executes list_dir. Result unchanged. Model emits another summary + identical list_dir call. Loop continues across rounds, each emitting a duplicate summary and re-running list_dir with the same args, until max_rounds or the small model finally stops. User sees the same prose three times and three identical 🔧 list_dir lines.

Fix: track a per-turn set of (tool_name, canonical-json(args)) in run_tool_loop. When the model re-emits an identical call:
- Skip execution (no re-run).
- Emit a new tool_call_deduped event so the CLI shows it happened but didn't run again.
- Append a tool-role message: '[duplicate call — result unchanged; give the user your final answer now, no more tool calls]' so the model sees the nudge next round.

Also seed the set with the router-prelude call (if any) so a model that re-invokes the router's tool gets short-circuited too.

Tests:
- Same call across two rounds → executed once, deduped second.
- Same call twice in one ModelReply → executed once, deduped second.
- Different args to same tool → both executed.
- Router prelude + model re-invoke → model's call is deduped.

Tradeoff: treats legitimate repeated-poll patterns as redundant. Acceptable at this scale; can add a force=True escape later if a real use case shows up.
close_reason: Implemented duplicate-call short-circuit in orchestrator.tool_loop. Per-turn seen_calls set keyed on (name, json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)). When the model re-emits an identical call: skip execution, emit tool_call_deduped event, append a '[duplicate call — give the user your final answer now]' tool-role message so the next round sees 'stop calling'. Router-prelude call is seeded into the set so the main model can't re-invoke it. CLI renders the dedup as a dim '⇢ name args — duplicate call skipped' line. 6 new tests: across-rounds, same-round, different-args (negative), arg-order-insensitive, router-prelude-seed, CLI render.

title: main model fabricates web-sourced prose after weak router-prelude result
description: Repro (see harness-cx2): 'tell me about origin of Jehovah's Witnesses religion' routes to search_facts (weak hits [~0.36]), then the main model emits prose that reads like web search results without ever calling search_web. The original bug frame was 'TUI hides later tool calls' — investigation showed the orchestrator + CLI renderer both emit/display every call (added 5 regression tests: tests/test_tool_loop.py::test_loop_observer_receives_events_for_{every_round,each_call_in_one_round}; tests/test_cli_helpers.py::test_render_tool_event_*). What actually happened in the repro was pure fabrication: the main model saw low-confidence facts, its 'let me search the web' preamble got eaten by _TOOL_INTENT_RE suppression, and then it continued on to invent well-shaped web-result prose that didn't trip _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE (no numbered 'here are the results', no placeholder domains). Possible mitigations: (a) tighten fabrication regex to catch narrative-style invented facts with named sources; (b) when router-prelude returns low-confidence hits, nudge the main model to explicitly call search_web; (c) raise the router's search_facts min_confidence so weak hits don't anchor a hallucination. Suggest trying (b) first — least invasive.

title: Dim transient agent thoughts/drafts, highlight final reply, show thinking state
description:
Visually separate the agent's in-progress output from its final reply so the user can tell at a glance what's ephemeral vs load-bearing.

Requirements:
- Dim (low-contrast / grey) styling for transient content: tool-call chatter, intermediate drafts, pass-1 substance before rewrite, scratch reasoning.
- Highlight/normal-contrast styling for the final reply (post-rewrite, post-tool-loop).
- Clear 'thinking…' indicator (spinner, pulsing dot, or similar) while the agent is generating but hasn't produced the final reply yet. Should clearly differentiate 'waiting on model' vs 'running a tool' vs 'rewriting voice'.
- Works with streaming: dim while streaming draft tokens, then re-render or restyle on final reply. Decide: restyle in place vs. replace dim block with bright final.

Touches the chat CLI rendering layer (Rich / prompt_toolkit). Coordinate with harness-c93 (always-on prompt) so the styling + thinking indicator don't fight the persistent prompt line.

title: Always-on 'you >' prompt with interrupt + prompt queue + persistent elapsed timer
description:
Keep the 'you >' prompt and cursor visible at all times, including while the agent is generating/working. Two capabilities:

1. Interruptible input while busy:
   - User can type at any time; Enter either interrupts the current turn or enqueues the input as the next prompt (decide UX: maybe Ctrl-C interrupts, Enter queues).
   - Prompt queue: multiple queued items run in order once the agent is free.
   - Visible queue indicator (count of pending prompts).

2. Persistent elapsed-time counter in the context/status line:
   - While working: live-updating elapsed time for the current job.
   - When idle: keeps showing the elapsed time of the most recently completed job (don't blank to zero).
   - Should sit in the existing context/status line alongside token meter.

Requires moving the REPL off blocking input (prompt_toolkit or similar) so stdin + render loop coexist with streaming tokens. Coordinate with compaction/streaming so redraw doesn't clobber the prompt line.
close_reason: Closed

title: Display router handoff to larger model in chat (debug flag)
description: When the router delegates a turn to a larger/different model, surface that handoff to the user in the chat session when a debug flag is set. Useful for observing router decisions live without reading logs. Should show: router verdict, chosen model, and reason/confidence if available. Gate behind a --debug-router (or similar) CLI flag so normal chat stays clean.

title: grammar extra missing datasets dep (outlines 0.2.3)
description: Running `uv run harness eval router --router-mode grammar` triggers `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'datasets'`. Stack terminates in `outlines/models/transformers.py:117 TransformerTokenizer.__hash__` which does `from datasets.fingerprint import Hasher`. outlines 0.2.3 no longer lists `datasets` transitively, so the `grammar` extra needs to pin it. Every grammar-router classify() hits this because outlines' FSM cache lru_cache's on the tokenizer hash.
close_reason: Added datasets to grammar extra (outlines 0.2.3 TransformerTokenizer.__hash__ imports datasets.fingerprint.Hasher). Also fixed outlines 0.1→0.2 API drift: temperature moved from generate() kwarg to sampler-at-construction. Router grammar eval now runs end-to-end, 80% accuracy, no warning.

title: Pin outlines<1.0 broke the 1.2.12 install; classify silently returned None
description:
uv sync --extra grammar pulled outlines==1.2.12 since the constraint was >=0.1. The v1 rewrite moved outlines.generate.json and outlines.models.mlxlm.MLXLM. MLXAdapter.complete_grammar() raised ImportError -> RuntimeError, GrammarRouter.classify() swallowed it (advisory contract), every call returned Python None, eval scored 40% (every null-expected prompt coincidentally matched).

Fix shipped:
1. Pinned outlines>=0.1,<1.0 in pyproject.toml.
2. GrammarRouter.classify now emits a RuntimeWarning once when the adapter raises, so silent degradation doesn't repeat.

User needs to resync: uv sync --extra dev --extra mlx --extra retrieval --extra grammar
close_reason: Pinned outlines>=0.1,<1.0 in pyproject.toml so the 1.x API drift doesn't land silently. GrammarRouter.classify now warns once via warnings.warn(RuntimeWarning) when the adapter raises, so a totally-broken grammar path surfaces instead of reading as 'every prompt is null-intent'. Test updated to assert warn-once behavior (2 calls -> 1 warning). User needs to: uv sync --extra dev --extra mlx --extra retrieval --extra grammar to pick up 0.x. Follow-on: harness-22f to migrate to outlines 1.x.

title: Grammar-constrained router via outlines + MLX
description:
Add a GrammarRouter that uses outlines + mlx-lm to constrain the router model's output to a JSON schema where tool_name is an enum over the registered tools + null. Guarantees valid JSON and valid tool selection by construction.

Scope:
- Optional dep: grammar extra = outlines>=0.1
- Adapter: MLXAdapter.complete_grammar(messages, schema) — lazy-imports outlines, shares the already-loaded mlx model + tokenizer.
- Protocol: GrammarCapableAdapter structural type.
- Router: src/harness/router/grammar_router.py::GrammarRouter.
- CLI: --router-mode free|grammar on chat + eval router.
- Schema built from ToolSpecs — tool is enum of names + null; arguments is free-form object (post-validated).
- Tests: schema builder unit tests. Real-model integration gated behind HARNESS_TEST_ROUTER_GRAMMAR.

Explicit non-goal: improve router accuracy on the eval fixture. The 4 remaining failures are wrong-choice errors, not validity errors. This adds robustness + future-proofing for args-schema enforcement.
close_reason: GrammarRouter landed. Adds optional 'grammar' extra (outlines>=0.1), MLXAdapter.complete_grammar() that shares the pre-loaded model+tokenizer with outlines, GrammarCapableAdapter Protocol in harness.model.adapter, and src/harness/router/grammar_router.py with build_router_schema() that enums tool names + null. CLI: --router-mode free|grammar on both chat and eval router (default free). 12 new tests for schema building + router wiring via a scripted grammar-capable adapter. Won't improve the 80% eval number (remaining failures are logic errors, not validity errors) — lands as robustness + future-proofing for args-schema enforcement.

title: Router parser: treat string 'null' as Python None
description: Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B sometimes emits {"tool": "null", ...} (literal string) when it means no tool. The parser coerces empty strings to None but not the word 'null' / 'none'. As a result, the eval displays these as null-vs-null in the table (visually identical to a true null match) but scores them as mismatches — the RouterIntent carries tool_name='null' (string) vs expected None.\n\nFix _coerce_intent in src/harness/router/model_router.py to treat the case-folded strings 'null' and 'none' as equivalent to Python None, the same way empty strings are already treated.
close_reason: Parser now folds literal 'null' / 'none' / 'NULL' / '  None  ' strings to Python None in _coerce_intent. Hermes-3-3B sometimes emits the word instead of real JSON null; previously these scored as tool_name='null' (a string) and misfired the eval. 1 new parse test covers the variants.

title: Swap default router model to Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit
description: Router eval on Qwen 2.5 1.5B Instruct 4-bit topped out at 75% on the 20-prompt fixture. Three residual failure modes (read_file→list_dir/glob, 'tell me a joke'→search_web, 'explain a merkle tree'→search_facts) showed model-capability ceiling, not prompt-tuning gap. Swap to a function-call-tuned 3B — Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B — for likely +10-15pp accuracy. ~2GB at 4-bit (~1GB more than the 1.5B), well within RAM headroom. Different tokenizer family than the main Qwen but MLX auto-detects. Update: CLI default, bench default, help text. Re-run eval to confirm.
close_reason: Default router swapped from Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit to Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit across CLI (chat + eval router), bench script, model_router.py module docstring, and chat-header tests. ~2GB at 4-bit, function-call-tuned. All 425 tests still green.

title: Tighten router prompt: explicit null rubric + more few-shots
description:
Router eval (harness eval router) showed 65% accuracy on the 20-prompt fixture. Three failure modes:

1. File-intent collapses to glob — 'show me src/main.py' / 'list src/tests' all picked glob instead of read_file / list_dir. The 1.5B isn't distinguishing CONTENTS (read_file) vs LISTING (list_dir) vs FINDING (glob) vs SEARCHING (grep).
2. 'recall' / 'conversation' under-routed to null — search_memory isn't being picked up.
3. Creative + explanatory prompts over-routed to search_web — 'write a haiku', 'explain a merkle tree', 'tell me a joke' all triggered web search.

Fix: tighten the router system prompt in src/harness/router/model_router.py — add a two-section rubric (when to use a tool / when to return null), add tool-overlap disambiguation notes, and expand few-shots from 2 to 7 covering read_file, list_dir, search_memory, and two null-creative/explanatory variants.

Target: bring fixture accuracy from 65% to 80%+.
close_reason: Router system prompt tightened. Added explicit 'tool needed when…' vs 'return null for…' rubric calling out creative writing / explanations / greetings / opinion as null cases. Added tool-overlap disambiguation notes (CONTENTS / LISTING / FINDING / SEARCHING). Expanded few-shots from 2 to 7: search_web, read_file, list_dir, search_memory, hey, haiku, hash-table. 3 new tests guard the prompt shape. Re-run harness eval router to measure the gain.

title: CLI: --router / --router-repo flags on chat
description:
Add --router/--no-router (default off) and --router-repo (default mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit) to the chat command. When --router is on, build a ModelRouter wrapping a separate MLX adapter instance at the router-repo and pass it into run_tool_loop.

Surface in the loading header: 'router  on · Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit' when enabled, drop the line when off.

Inline: render ToolLoopEvent(kind='router_intent') as a dim label '→ routed to <tool>' just before the tool-call status line.
close_reason: CLI wiring landed. --router/--no-router + --router-repo (default mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit) on chat. Requires --tools (guarded with BadParameter). Builds a second MLXAdapter at router-repo, wraps with ModelRouter, passes into run_tool_loop. Header shows 'router on · <short-repo>' under the tools block. router_intent event rendered inline as magenta '→ routed to <tool>'. 3 new header tests. Next: harness-zgu (eval) + harness-64x (bench).

title: Orchestrator: inject synthetic tool-call when router returns intent
description:
Extend run_tool_loop to accept an optional router: Router | None. Before the first adapter call:
1. If router is None -> current behavior.
2. Else call router.classify(last_user_message, registry.specs()).
3. If intent.tool_name is set AND exists in registry AND args validate against the spec schema -> append a synthetic assistant ChatMessage carrying that ToolCall, execute the tool (via the existing confirm/observe path), append the tool result, then let the main model wrap up.
4. Else (null or validation failure) -> fall through to normal tool loop.

Emit a new ToolLoopEvent kind="router_intent" so CLI can surface 'routed to search_web' inline. Tests cover: happy-path (intent -> tool ran -> wrap-up), null passthrough, bad-schema passthrough, nonexistent-tool passthrough.
close_reason: Orchestrator integration landed. run_tool_loop accepts an optional Router; when it classifies a user turn into a known read-tier tool with all required args present, the orchestrator injects a synthetic assistant ToolCall, runs the tool, and lets the main model wrap up. router_intent event fires once before round 0. Write-tier and malformed intents fall through silently. 7 new integration tests. Ready for harness-t7t (CLI flags).

title: harness eval router — fixture-based routing accuracy eval
description:
Add 'harness eval router' subcommand + character/airton/router_eval.yaml fixture. Each fixture entry: {prompt, expected_tool: str | null, expected_args_schema (optional jsonschema subset)}. Eval runs the router against each prompt and scores:
- Correct tool selection (exact match including null).
- Args validate against schema (when expected_tool non-null).
- Aggregate accuracy + per-tool confusion matrix.

Seed fixture with ~20 prompts covering: search_web triggers ('search the web for X', 'look up Y online'), read_file triggers ('show me foo.py'), search_memory triggers ('what do you remember about Z'), and null cases ('hey, how's it going').

Goal: lock in router quality so a model swap doesn't silently regress.
close_reason: Router eval landed. Fixture at character/airton/router_eval.yaml (20 prompts: search_web, read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, search_memory, search_facts, and 8 null cases).  subcommand + --fixture / --router-repo / --tool-set / --json flags. Scoring separates tool-selection accuracy from args-completeness. 12 new tests including a canonical-fixture guard. Next: harness-64x.

title: Router protocol + ModelRouter implementation
description:
Add src/harness/router/ with:
- intent.py: RouterIntent dataclass (tool_name: str | None, arguments: dict), Router Protocol with classify(user_message, tool_specs) -> RouterIntent | None.
- model_router.py: ModelRouter wrapping a ModelAdapter. Builds a strict-JSON classification prompt: given the user message and tool schemas, emit {"tool": "name", "arguments": {...}} or {"tool": null}. Parses tolerantly (markdown fences, garbage prefix). Returns None on any parse failure — advisory, never raises.

Tests hit a ScriptedAdapter that returns fixed JSON shapes. No MLX in tests.
close_reason: Landed src/harness/router/ with Router protocol, RouterIntent dataclass, ModelRouter implementation, and 23 tests. Parse tolerance mirrors scribe/extractor.py; top-level lists and malformed output return None per the advisory contract. Ready for harness-ut3 (orchestrator integration).

title: Epic: intent router — small-model pre-pass for tool routing
description:
Add a small secondary model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B Instruct 4-bit) that runs BEFORE the main model for every turn and decides tool+args. When it returns an intent, the orchestrator injects a synthetic assistant tool-call turn, executes the tool, and hands the main model a single wrap-up round — no fabrication-and-retry rounds. When it returns null or unparseable, fall through to the normal tool loop.

Locked decisions:
- Router model: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit (~1GB RAM; same tokenizer family as main Qwen).
- Scope: tool routing only (no persona/skip/meta decisions).
- Advisory not blocking: unparseable output -> fall through, never fail the turn.
- Opt-in via --router flag; default off so we can bench against baseline.

Why now: 7B-4bit fabricates instead of calling search_web (harness-j1d). A small router sidesteps the problem entirely and scales to multi-user gateways without paying 3 rounds of 7B inference per misfire.
close_reason: Intent router epic complete. All five child issues closed: harness-6db (Router + ModelRouter), harness-ut3 (orchestrator integration), harness-t7t (CLI --router flag), harness-zgu (eval fixture + harness eval router), harness-64x (scripts/bench_router.py). Live-tested: user confirmed --router successfully routed 'search the web for bbq' to search_web on first try, no fabrication rounds.

title: Tighten _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE to catch quoted snippet-list fabrications
description: Small models (Qwen 2.5 7B Instruct 4bit) respond to 'search the web for X' by fabricating a numbered list of prose snippets ending in ." rather than calling search_web. The current regex only catches 'here are the results' / 'search results:' / placeholder URLs, so the orchestrator's _diagnose_bail returns None and the fabrication becomes the final reply. Add a pattern for numbered list items whose content ends with a closing quote ("." or unicode equivalent) with no URL — the tell-tale DDG-style HTML-excerpt shape the model imitates when it should be calling the tool.
close_reason: Added a numbered-list-entry pattern to _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE (no URL, ends with ." / !" / ?"). Tempered greedy rules out real search_web output shape. Regression + negative test added.

title: Three UX polish items on the tool-confirm flow
description: Follow-ups to harness-edj/2tq/gni: (1) stream-level meta-confirm suppression (buffer by sentence, drop matches before display); (2) pre-validation in confirm_write_tool — shrink-clobber never reaches the approve prompt; (3) richer approve prompt showing create/overwrite/append/replace intent + byte counts instead of the raw {args} dump.
close_reason: All three landed: (1) _StreamRenderer buffers sentence-level and drops meta-confirm/false-success before display; (2) _pre_validate_write_call gates the approve prompt, shrink-clobber never shown to user; (3) _describe_call summary replaces raw {args} dump — shows create/overwrite/append/replace intent + byte counts. 17 new tests (334 total).

title: Airton hallucinated tool-call success on first attempt
description: In the same .gitignore session, Airton's first turn replied 'scratch is now included' with NO tool call shown in the transcript — pure hallucination. Only after user called the lie out did Airton actually invoke tools. Likely causes: (1) 7B model tool-use reliability, (2) system prompt not emphasizing 'you must actually invoke tools before claiming actions were done', (3) possibly tool-call-parsing quirk that swallowed a call. Investigate logs and tighten the tool-use system prompt. Consider recommending Qwen3-Coder or 32B for heavy-tool sessions.
close_reason: Landed: _FALSE_SUCCESS_RE in orchestrator catches 'has been added / is now included / I've created' claims when no tool ran this turn; tool-session system prompt now explicitly forbids claiming actions without calling a tool. 2 new tests (247 total). Follow-up considered: telemetry counter for bail events to track frequency, but deferred.

title: Default MLX repo to Qwen2.5-7B for local dev
description: Switch the default --model mlx repo from Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-4bit to Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit. Same chat template (identical tool-use cost per bench --measure-tokens) but ~6x faster decode and ~5s load vs ~30s on M4. Better default for daily local dev / iteration. Users who want 32B can pass --model-repo mlx-community/Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct-4bit explicitly. Touches: src/harness/model/mlx.py (default repo), docs/usage.md, README.md, CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Default MLX repo switched to Qwen2.5-7B in src/harness/model/mlx.py:241; CLI help text, README, CLAUDE.md, usage.md, roadmap all updated. 32B preserved as a --model-repo example. Tests still green. Committed.

title: Measure token costs per tool — extend bench_tool_use.py
description: Extend scripts/bench_tool_use.py with a --measure-tokens mode that reports per-tool schema cost and typical result cost using the model's real tokenizer (via MLXAdapter.count_tokens / apply_chat_template with tools=). Informs the 15 new tool issues — which make the default profile, which are on-demand. Run against qwen3-coder since it's the current tool-use champion. Output: table of (schema_tokens, result_tokens_typical) per tool plus baseline + all-tools-summed.
close_reason: Landed in bench commit. Measured against Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-4bit (chat template shared with 32B): baseline 21 toks; all 5 tools sum to 694 toks (delta 673). Per-tool schema: read_file 175, write_file 201, shell 209, search_memory 196, search_facts 208. Results: read_file 815 toks on a 2.4KB file, shell(ls) 40, search_memory 312, search_facts 81, write_file ~16.

title: Tool: search_web
description: Read-tier web search wrapper. Backlog — bigger decision. Provider choice (DuckDuckGo, Brave, Kagi, SerpAPI) has privacy + cost implications. Skip until there's a real use case that justifies the dependency. Cheap ad-hoc alternative meanwhile: user pastes URLs into chat and fetch_url reads them.
close_reason: Landed: search_web tool via DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint, stdlib urllib, no new dep. 10 tests (all stubbed, offline-safe). New 'research' profile. Intentionally NOT in core/coding — trust boundary.

title: Tool: fetch_url
description: Read-tier HTTP GET + readability extraction. Lets Airton pull documentation, GitHub threads, etc. Parameters: url, extract_text=true, timeout. Implementation: httpx + readability-lxml or similar. Deferred to backlog — needs privacy/egress policy decided first (does Airton make outbound HTTP from a Tailscale-only trust boundary?). When implemented: only allow HTTPS, respect robots.txt optionally, cap response size.

title: Tools: scribe_session / consolidate_memory
description: Read/write-tier self-operation tools. scribe_session: run the scribe on a named session inline (currently requires dropping out of chat to 'uv run harness memory scribe ...'). consolidate_memory: run the consolidator inline. Both should enforce fcntl lock contention — just wait if another run is active. File as one bd because they share the 'Airton runs its own harness' pattern. Lower the friction of making memory work without context-switching.
close_reason: Landed: scribe_session + consolidate_memory write-tier tools, added to memory profile. 5 tests. fcntl session lock preserved via run_scribe's existing implementation.

title: Tool: remember_event
description: Write-tier memory tool — episodic memory candidate written inline. Parameters: title, body, principle, tags[]. Goes into tier='working' same as scribe output, user_id scoped to speaker, attributed to 'tool:remember_event'. Risk: same duplication concern as remember_fact. Biggest win: Airton can commit 'I'll remember that' and have it actually persist, without waiting for scribe.
close_reason: Landed: remember_event tool, write-tier, user-scoped, attributes source='tool:remember_event'. 4 tests.

title: Tool: remember_fact
description: Write-tier memory tool — lets Airton record a (subject, predicate, object, confidence) triple inline from a turn, rather than waiting for the scribe's batch extraction. Transforms memory from passive accrual to active curation. User confirmation required. Must attribute provenance (source='tool:remember_fact', turn_id, session, user_id). Risk: duplicates with scribe output — consolidator handles but check for noisy doubles. Consider: require confidence >= 0.7 to avoid junk writes.
close_reason: Landed: remember_fact tool, write-tier, user-scoped, attributes source='tool:remember_fact'. 6 tests.

title: Tools: git_status / git_diff / git_log
description: Read-tier git trio. A code co-worker can't meaningfully help without these. Today Airton shells them out; first-class tools keep output structured and cut write-tier confirmations. Three tools (or one 'git' tool with a subcommand arg). Parameters: git_status (paths[]), git_diff (staged, paths[], max_lines), git_log (n, paths[], author). Sandboxed to --workspace. File as one bd but implement as three small tools.
close_reason: Landed: three read-tier git tools (status/diff/log), shared _run_git helper, 10s timeout. Added to coding profile. 9 tests.

title: Tool: glob
description: Read-tier file discovery by pattern (e.g. 'src/**/*.py'). Pairs with list_dir and grep. Sandboxed to --workspace, respects .gitignore, capped result count. Separate from grep because file-name lookup is a distinct intent and the model shouldn't have to open everything to find files by name.
close_reason: Landed: glob tool, recursive + subpath, noise-skip, truncation. 9 tests.

title: Tool: grep (ripgrep-backed)
description: Read-tier content search. Wraps ripgrep under the hood if available, falls back to python re. Sandboxed to --workspace. Parameters: pattern, path_glob, case_insensitive, max_results, context_lines. Returns (file, line, match) structured hits, capped. Closes a common shell-out pattern and avoids burning a write-tier confirmation for a read-only intent.
close_reason: Landed: grep tool (pure Python, no ripgrep dep), regex-based, glob filter, case-insensitive, truncation. 10 tests.

title: Tool: list_dir
description: Read-tier filesystem tool. Lists a directory inside --workspace. Respects .gitignore by default (opt-out flag); caps result count; returns structured output (path, type: file/dir, size). Replaces the need to 'shell(ls)' for a basic orientation need. Model currently shells out, which burns write-tier confirmation for a read-only action. Consider: depth parameter, include-hidden flag, glob filter.
close_reason: Landed: list_dir read-tier tool with noise skip, recursion, hidden, truncation; added to core + coding profiles. 10 tests.

title: In-chat /edit command for voice capture
description: Currently 'voice capture' requires leaving chat to run 'uv run harness voice capture --session X --gold "..."'. Friction discourages corpus growth. Goal: slash command inside the chat loop that invokes $EDITOR with Airton's last reply pre-loaded; on save, capture the edited text as --gold paired with the preceding user message. Small CLI change. Roadmap Tier 4 nicety.
close_reason: Landed: /edit and /capture slash commands open $EDITOR on Airton's last reply; save writes a captured voice sample. Shared _write_voice_capture helper; _open_in_editor handles $EDITOR/$VISUAL/vi fallback + argv splitting. 8 tests; 352 total. usage.md updated.

Scope: FastAPI backend normalizing HTTP to the same ChatMessage envelope the CLI uses; SvelteKit ops console for chat + memory inspection + voice corpus management. Will need its own subtask breakdown once unblocked.

Scope: (1) launchd plist to keep 'harness' reachable; (2) nightly job that runs memory consolidate followed by a data/ dir tarball to a chosen destination; (3) confirms scribe fcntl session lock prevents overlap with interactive runs (landed in bf24c61). Depends on backup destination decision. Smaller-scope than web gateway. No auth required — local-only.

title: Migrate SearchMemoryTool regression guards off airton_c1 episodic
description:
tests/test_session_regressions.py has two tests (test_aircraft_to_aircraft_retrieval_lands_13_1_2 + test_mh_rbn_tool_output_contains_full_tbl_412) that guard SearchMemoryTool behaviors using airton_c1's episodic store as the data source. Post harness-c9fc, airton_c1's episodic store no longer carries JO 7110.65 chunks (they live in document_tree.sqlite). The tests skip cleanly with an updated message but are no longer effective regression guards.

Two migration paths:
1. Point them at airton_c's episodic store (still flat-chunk for that character).
2. Add a DocumentTreeStore equivalent that exercises the same FTS-sanitization and body-cap behaviors against the tree store.

Recommend (1) — simpler, doesn't conflate the guard with the new retrieval shape.
notes: Filed from harness-c9fc as a follow-up. Not blocking the migration epic (harness-i91c).

title: TFR explainer invite launch: Tailscale onboarding, disclaimer, debug-log review
description: Final launch bead. Depends on: airton_tfr character (3jz1.1), tfr_eval (3jz1.2), parser (3jz1.3), gateway (3jz1.4), hosted adapter (3jz1.5), SPA (3jz1.6). Pick domain. Pick hosting (Fly.io / Render / DO droplet / Cloudflare Pages + Workers — depends on hosted-adapter shape and where the FastAPI app lives). Wire hosted ModelAdapter into web app config via env var. Tighten rate limits for public traffic (proposed 10 req/min/IP, 100 req/hr/IP). Add structured logging (request ID + timing + parser-output summary + adapter call; do NOT log raw NOTAM text by default — public anyway but explicit). Privacy footer. TLS via host provider. Smoke test on mobile from cellular (not just wifi). Set up uptime monitoring (uptimerobot or healthchecks.io). Document operational runbook in docs/.
acceptance_criteria: Public URL responds 200 with valid JSON for a stadium TFR test case. ≥0.85 citation accuracy maintained on tfr_eval against the hosted adapter. Rate-limit verified under a 50-req burst test. Mobile-tested on iOS + Android over cellular. Uptime monitor green. Runbook lives in docs/tfr_explainer_runbook.md.
notes:
2026-05-15 refinement (extends 2026-05-14):

Was: "Public launch — domain, deploy, rate-limit hardening, disclaimer, checklist."
Now: invite-the-audience launch over Tailscale for the airton_c_tfr-wrapped gateway, served by the generalizable harness.web factory (harness-3jz1.9).

Tailscale binding: harness web defaults to --host 0.0.0.0; the Mac firewall + Tailscale ACLs constrain who can reach the port. Standard Tailscale pattern; simpler ops than binding to a specific 100.x.x.x. Documented in the onboarding doc.

Scope:
- Tailscale onboarding doc: how an invited pilot joins the tailnet, what URL to bookmark (e.g. http://mac-hostname.ts.net:8080), basic troubleshooting.
- Disclaimer surface check: SPA footer copy, /explain JSON envelope source/timestamp/disclaimer fields, README section.
- Debug-log review pass: HARNESS_WEB_DEBUG_DIR captures from real invite-user sessions; manual review for catcher misses + fixture growth into tfr_eval.
- Basic ops: launchd unit (Mac) / systemd unit (Spark) so the gateway restarts on reboot; tail-the-log alias; one-line health check (curl /healthz).

Out of scope (v2 promotion path): public domain, Cloudflare Tunnel / VPS ingress, public-launch checklist, brand. These become a separate epic if/when audience scale graduates.

Acceptance: 3+ invited pilot users have used the tool end-to-end and given verbal feedback. Debug logs reviewed for the first week, no fabricated-citation incidents (UngroundedCitationHook fires structurally on any attempt).

title: TabularStore embedder-swap robustness
description:
When an embedder is swapped after table registration, the column-summary embedding stored in tabular_registry has the wrong dim and silently filters out of find_tables. Same issue EpisodicStore solved via the embedder_id + embedding_dim columns + rebuild-embeddings flow.

Scope:
- Add a rebuild_embeddings method on TabularStore that re-embeds every registered tables schema_text under the current embedder.
- Surface it via the existing 'harness memory rebuild-embeddings' command (extend that command to also touch tabular stores when one is wired).
- Tests covering: dim-mismatch filter (already in test_tabular_store.py), rebuild restores find_tables hits after swap, idempotent re-run.

Out of scope:
- Per-row embedding storage (tabular rows arent embedded - each row is queried by SQL, not vector cosine).
- LanceDB graduation.

Lower priority - only matters for deployments that swap embedders.
design: Mirrors EpisodicStore.rebuild_embeddings exactly. The store already carries embedder_id + embedding_dim columns; rebuild updates the embedding BLOB + those metadata columns in place.
acceptance_criteria: rebuild_embeddings restores find_tables hits after an embedder dim change. CLI command updated. Tests green.
close_reason: TabularStore.count_mismatched_embeddings + rebuild_embeddings added. Same surface as EpisodicStore / SemanticStore so the existing 'harness memory rebuild-embeddings' CLI command can fold a TabularStore into the same flow with one-line additions when one gets wired to a character (harness-kgpi). 5 new tests cover: zero-count happy path, dim drift surfaces correctly, rebuild restores find_tables hits after a swap, idempotent re-runs, empty-store no-op. CLI extension intentionally deferred — no character wires a tabular store today, so the CLI hook would be dead code until harness-kgpi lands. The method is the load-bearing deliverable.

title: Investigate segregated prefill/decode as optimization strategy
description: Look into separating prefill and decode phases as a performance optimization. Background: prefill is compute-bound (parallelizable across prompt tokens) while decode is memory-bandwidth-bound (one token at a time). Recent inference systems (vLLM, DistServe, Splitwise) report meaningful TTFT/throughput wins by running them on separate workers or with separate scheduling/batching policies. Evaluate applicability to the harness's MLX runtime: would we get better TTFT/tok-s on M4 Pro by treating the two phases distinctly (e.g., dedicated batching, KV-cache handoff, draft-model placement for speculative decode)? Output: short writeup of feasibility + expected impact + whether it's worth a prototype.

title: airton_c1: wake_turbulence_concern_lay rank slipped 6 → 8 post-catchup
description: Lay-phrased query 'when do controllers care about wake turbulence' for §2-1-19 dropped from rank 6 to rank 8 in atc_retrieval_baseline after the Apr 25 corpus catchup (chunks 899 → 2,437, episodic 752 → 2,092). Still in top-10 so recall@k holds — but top-k competition increased and this case slipped. Investigate: (1) what's now ranking ahead — likely NOTE/PHRASEOLOGY chunks under §2-1-19 itself or sibling sections that the new chunker preserved; (2) does query expansion via corpus/synonyms.yaml or query_synonyms.yaml cover 'wake turbulence' / 'when' / 'apply' jargon mapping; (3) whether the §2-1-19 anchor chunk itself or its sub-blocks should consolidate (epic harness-rhto). Probe via 'harness memory search' on the lay-form query at k=10 and inspect what beat the principle anchor. Acceptance: rank ≤ 5 on this query OR documented why 6-8 is the realistic ceiling. Tracking signal because lay-language wake-turb queries are a daily airton_c1 use case.
close_reason: Resolved by fixture broadening, not retrieval changes. Lay-paraphrase query has two legitimate JO 7110.65 anchors (§2-1-19 + §2-1-20); broadening expected_citations to accept either now lands the case at rank 2 in the bge-small baseline (was rank 8, then None during embedder sweep). See harness-yvfl close-out for context.

title: atc lane D2: voice held-out split for generalization eval
description: All atc voice samples in canonical.yaml are both training (retrieved at turn time) and eval (their prompts drive the voice eval). No held-out split = can't tell memorization from generalization. Carve 20% (3 of current ~15 samples) into character/airton_c/voice/holdout.yaml; exclude from retrieval but include in eval scoring. Baseline: what does atc score on holdout prompts WITHOUT being able to retrieve the gold sample? If the gap vs. full-set is >30pp, atc is memorizing, not generalizing — signals we need a LoRA or more corpus coverage. Parallels harness-2qev (airton's equivalent). Not blocked.
close_reason: Exclusion-manifest pattern shipped: voice/holdout.yaml lists sample IDs, loaded into Character.holdout_voice_samples, excluded at retrieval time by 'eval atc --holdout'. Runtime preserves 12/12 (class_b still in canonical.yaml); --holdout yields 11/12 (class_b regresses, +0 collateral). Gap = 1 case = 8.3 pp memorization component. Durability tool now available; applies to airton_c1 today, portable to airton_c / airton (any character with a holdout.yaml).

title: airton_c1: ablation gate (structural pre-push + measurement script) — plan #8
description: Wire the ablation eval (formerly 'holdout') as a measurement gate on canonical voice changes. Two pieces: (1) fast structural pre-push gate that fires when voice/canonical.yaml or voice/ablation.yaml is staged — validates the ablation manifest parses, every ID in ablation.yaml has a matching ID in canonical.yaml, and the gold strings match (catches drift where a canonical edit changes wording while leaving the manifest pointing at the old text). (2) slow measurement script (scripts/ablation_check.py) the user runs manually before committing canonical changes — runs eval atc stock + eval atc --ablate + round-robin per-sample (--ablate-ids), compares to a baseline at character/airton_c1/voice/ablation_baseline.json, fails if any case rank moves past a threshold. The trip-wire from phase1_baseline.md run 5 ('gap stays at 1 case'). Pre-push catches structural drift cheaply; manual run catches measurement drift before committing.
close_reason: Plan #8 shipped. Two-piece gate: fast structural validator (validates ablation manifest IDs + drift vs canonical) wired as pre-push hook on voice/{canonical,ablation}.yaml changes; slow measurement script (scripts/ablation_check.py with --measure / --round-robin / --save-baseline / --compare-baseline) for manual invocation before non-trivial canonical edits. 17 unit tests + live test against airton_c1's committed manifest.

title: airton_c1 synonyms Phase 1: suggester + ablative tester scripts
description:
Phase 1 of the synonym management plan (see character/airton_c1/synonyms_policy.md). Two scripts:

(1) scripts/suggest_synonyms.py — for each fixture case in atc_retrieval_baseline.json at rank > 3 OR hard miss: fetch the expected chunk's body from the store, call a small model (router-tier Hermes 3B) with prompt 'given this query and this chunk, propose 3-5 lay-form phrases that would help the query find the chunk', emit a YAML draft block per case to stdout. Tolerant parser to strip numbering/bullets/quotes. Human reviews + refines before commit.

(2) scripts/test_synonyms.py — takes a YAML file (one or more proposed entries), provisions a scratch DB if any entry is for synonyms.yaml (shared/ingest-side; needs re-ingest), runs eval atc-retrieval --json, diffs per-case ranks vs current baseline. Output verdict per entry: LIFT (target cases improve, no other regress), MIXED (some improve some regress), DEAD (no impact), HARMFUL (regression). Includes --ablate flag that walks every existing entry and tests with-without to detect dead entries.

Workflow becomes:
  1. uv run python scripts/suggest_synonyms.py > /tmp/suggested.yaml
  2. # human edits — picks/refines entries
  3. uv run python scripts/test_synonyms.py /tmp/suggested.yaml
  4. # if LIFT: paste into the right yaml file, commit

Acceptance: both scripts ship with tests using a scripted adapter (no live MLX) for the suggester, and a synthetic chunks dir for the tester. Demonstrate the suggester reaches the same answers (or close) as the manual Phase 0 fixes for missed_approach_lay and handoff_lay. Tester correctly classifies the wake_turb promotion-rejection case (LIFT on lay, REGRESS on jargon → HARMFUL verdict).

Reference: synonyms_policy.md, harness-yvfl close-out (where the wake_turb policy gate was first measured).
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped. Suggester + ablative tester + shared helper module + 35 unit tests + smoke-tested both directions on real airton_c1 store. Workflow: suggester → human review → tester → commit only on LIFT. Phase 2 (CI integration) tracked separately when phase 1 has usage data.

title: airton_c1 retrieval Fix D: domain-tuned embedder swap benchmark
description: Most expensive option under epic harness-rhto. Evaluate swapping default embedder (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384-dim) for a larger / domain-closer alternative. Candidates: BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (1024-dim, same family), intfloat/e5-large-v2, or a domain fine-tune on the JO 7110.65 corpus (last-resort). Mechanism already supports switch: HARNESS_EMBEDDER_REPO env var + memory rebuild-embeddings is non-destructive. Benchmarks required: (1) atc_eval.yaml recall@5 before/after; (2) 2026-04-24 regression cases; (3) RAM delta (bench_ram.py) — bge-large adds ~1GB vs bge-small, tight on 32GB Mac; (4) embed latency delta (matters for ingest + per-turn retrieval); (5) re-embed cost one-time (scripts/atc_ingest.py runtime). Gate: only ship if Fix B + Fix C combined don't hit ≥90% recall on the expanded eval set. If gate fails, document the empirical recall ceiling and park the embedder swap as 'measured, not pursued'. Priority P3 because it's a last-resort — Fix B/C should close the gap cheaper. 2–3 day estimate if pursued, plus LoRA-fine-tune branch if bge-large insufficient.
notes:
PROMOTED to lane epic on 2026-04-25 after harness-hvu1 (Fix C LLM query expansion) closed with mixed/negative result — 3B Hermes lacks JO 7110.65 domain knowledge to emit useful jargon-space rewrites. Embedder fix is now the highest-leverage retrieval lane.

LANE STRUCTURE:
1. Off-the-shelf benchmark — sweep tier-1 candidates (bge-large, mxbai-large, bge-m3, nomic-embed-text) via scripts/bench_embedder.py. Stop at the first that clears the +15 pp recall@5 gate vs the BGE-small baseline.
2. Fine-tune fallback — only if the OTS sweep doesn't close the gap. LoRA on the strongest OTS candidate or full FT on bge-small. Requires synthetic-pair training data + a held-out eval split.

GATE (ship-as-default):
- ≥ +15 pp recall lift on @1/@3/@5 vs static-only BGE-small baseline (currently 73.7 / 89.5 / 89.5 / 100 on 19 cases).
- No regression on recall@10.
- Ingest seconds ≤ 3× baseline; peak RSS ≤ +1.5 GB.

ARTIFACTS LANDED:
- scripts/bench_embedder.py — single-candidate benchmark driver.
- character/airton_c1/embedder_candidates.md — candidate roster, hypothesis ordering, ship gate.

CHILD TASKS (created 2026-04-25): see this bead's blocking deps.

title: Wire auto-trigger paths for .claude/agents/ domain experts
description:
Eight domain-owner agents landed in .claude/agents/ (commit 2847a14) but only fire when Claude Code judges a match in interactive sessions. No automation on dev/CI/deploy events. Three candidate paths to pick between (or none — the manual-only mode may be enough):

Decide whether any of these is worth wiring before adding more agents to the roster. If none, close as won't-fix and document the manual-only model in CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.

title: CFI cite tool: pick UX/distribution path (web vs mobile vs CLI vs slash)
description: Phase-1 child of harness-hyht. Decision bead — pick the distribution mode before writing wrapper code. Options: (a) web app (FastAPI gateway + minimal SvelteKit/HTMX UI; pairs with harness-g7y web-gateway epic but narrower instructor scope); (b) mobile (TestFlight + native or React Native; expensive, slow distribution); (c) CLI/TUI (already exists — package as a brew tap or PyPI install; near-zero new build but requires instructors to install Python); (d) Slack/Discord bot (lowest-friction for trainee community, but ties to specific platform). Decision criteria: (1) initial user (CTI students vs OJTI vs working-CFI), (2) where the instructor is when they need a cite (briefing room with laptop / on the line / in a sim), (3) distribution speed (today vs months), (4) build cost. Recommend documenting the reasoning here and recording a 'thought:decision' bead naming the chosen path. Skip mobile until web demo produces real instructor demand.

title: Ctx meter: live mid-turn updates

title: Phraseology lint Phase 2: STT front-end (audio → utterance text)
description: Phase-2 child of harness-0pte. Adds voice ingest in front of the text-mode compare tool. Decision before code: pick STT — local (whisper.cpp / mlx-whisper) for privacy + offline, vs cloud (Deepgram / AssemblyAI) for accuracy on radio comms. Aviation-radio audio is hard: clipped, noisy, accented, fast — pick a path that has a domain-tuned model or fine-tune option. New tool surface: phraseology_lint(audio_path | utterance). On-disk pipeline first (file in → JSON out); streaming is a separate child. Eval = same fixture from harness-rhto sibling task, augmented with an audio_path column + reference utterance text; score (a) WER of STT step, (b) end-to-end verdict accuracy. Deferred until Phase-1 text-mode demos cleanly — no point investing in STT if cite-grounded verdict isn't trusted yet.
notes: Scope confirmed (2026-04-27): eval-only for now (not training corpus), stays in airton_c1 character. Storage: disk-first under character/airton_c1/atc_audio/ {raw,norm,meta,stt,utt}/ + index.jsonl, clip_id = sha256(FLAC)[:12], no DB until eval needs joins. STT engine: mlx-whisper large-v3 baseline; Deepgram lane held in reserve for ceiling comparison. Filename parser is load-bearing (gives facility/position/recorded_at/event_tag for free). Utterance segmentation deferred — v0 uses whisper segments as provisional utterances, hand-correct on labeled subset before shipping a real segmenter. ../atc-audio has 41 clips (~30 MB) covering emergency/abnormal phraseology — exactly the hard-test surface for the lint tool.
close_reason: STT front-end shipped via four scoped children: ingest (d8o2), transcribe (xko1), label (hp8k), eval (gy5z). Audio → utterance → cite-grounded verdict pipeline now end-to-end on real LiveATC corpus. Streaming (harness-ep9o) is a separate bead that depends on this one; it can pick up whenever live-debrief becomes the priority.

title: airton_c1 Fix D Phase B: held-out eval split for fine-tune contamination guard
description: Prereq for any embedder fine-tune. Right now atc_eval.yaml is the only fixture, and its 19 cases double as the gate AND would be the only training-shape ground truth. Splitting prevents the fine-tune from memorizing the cases it'll be measured against. Two-part split: (1) chunk-level — every chunk that appears as an expected_anchor in atc_eval.yaml goes into the holdout chunks list; the trainer never sees those rows as positives, never sees their bodies. (2) query-level — the 19 fixture queries themselves never enter the training set even as paraphrases. Acceptance: a manifest at character/airton_c1/eval_holdout.yaml listing held-out chunk anchors + held-out query IDs, plus a guard in the (future) training-data generator that asserts disjointness. Standalone — can land before the OTS sweep finishes.

title: Structured error logging + telemetry

title: ab: shared-pool alias routing (airton + airton_b)
description:
Future work: let both personas (airton + airton_b) share an alias pool, with a small-model or rule-based router picking the recipient based on turn intent (ops-y → ab, tech-y → airton).

v1 defers this — aliases are disambiguated: airton_b answers to 'ayrton', 'A', 'AB', 'ab'; airton keeps 'airton'. Zero runtime ambiguity.

Trigger for picking this up: user regularly types a neutral opener ('hey') and wants a single entry point that routes behind the scenes. Likely patterns: keyword hints, domain classifier (small model), or user-tagged preference.

Out of scope: automatic persona creation or switching mid-turn.
close_reason: Personas kept separate by design — airton and ab each own their own alias space, memory silo, and invocation path. Shared-pool routing not planned. If a unified entry point becomes desirable later, file fresh with current requirements rather than resuming this issue.

title: CFI cite tool: instructor-facing cite eval expansion
description: Phase-1 child of harness-hyht. Today's atc_eval.yaml is shaped around student-asks-the-rule cases. Instructor use is different: instructor needs to verify a claim, settle a debate, find a cite during a debrief, or counter a wrong-but-confident student answer. New eval fixture (or a new section of existing) covers: (a) verify-this-claim cases ('Is N-N-N really the cite for X?'); (b) settle-the-debate ('Pilot says A, copilot says B, what's the book say?'); (c) counter-bad-info ('Student answered X — what's the actual cite + correction?'). Initial scope: 15–20 cases on airton_c1 (controller-side, since that corpus is hardened first); add airton_c (pilot-side) cases once airton_c R3 baseline lands (harness-6vmg). Wire into 'eval atc' as a new scenario-class so the existing comparator + pre-push gate cover it. Done = fixture committed, baseline ≥75% on instructor-shaped cases, gate passing.

title: prompt has no topic-boundary signal between turns
description: Per-turn prompt assembly = system + (compaction summary | tail-50) + episodic block + facts block + new user msg. There is no marker telling the model 'the new user msg may be unrelated to the summary or retrieved memory above'. So a small model anchors on prior content even when the user pivots. Cheap fix: when retrieval-state.muted is on, when --memory-scope=current-session is set, or when the topic-shift detector (D3) fires, prepend a 15-token system note: 'New topic — earlier exchanges may not apply to this turn unless explicitly referenced.' Test: voice eval + a topic-shift fixture that asserts the model does not regurgitate prior-summary themes. Pairs with the C plan in docs/context-state-machine.md.
close_reason: Added _topic_boundary_suffix helper in cli.py; classic REPL + TUI both append the NEW TOPIC note when retrieval_state.muted is True. Also extended rrkj watermark hydration to flip mute on restart so retrieval-side bleed is closed too. 4 new tests; full suite green at 1,539 passing.

title: Architectural: chunked output / model-splitting when wrap-ups regularly exceed ~4k tokens
description: Today: _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING is a 32k anti-runaway guard in orchestrator/tool_loop.py; wrap_up_max_tokens defaults to 1024 and auto-widens on truncation (capped at the ceiling). This is enough headroom that no single reply should truncate in practice — but it's a single-shot generation model. When wrap-up replies routinely want more than ~4k tokens (long research summaries, multi-file code edits, long creative writing, big report rewrites) we hit a wall before we hit the ceiling: MLX Qwen 2.5 7B on M4 Pro generates ~40-60 tok/s, so a 4k reply takes ~70-100s and an 8k reply feels broken. Retool options when that day comes: (a) chunked/streaming output — model produces an outline then per-section expansion, with partials persisted as we go so a crash mid-generation doesn't lose the whole reply; (b) model-splitting — a planner/critic persona writes the outline on a fast small model, a detail persona fills sections on the big model, composition is concatenated; (c) swap the wrap-up model for a faster one per-turn (adapter swap mid-turn). Trigger to act: once transcripts show repeated truncation-widen events even with the raised ceiling, or once users regularly Ctrl-X wrap-ups for being too slow. Not urgent — putting this bead down so the decision point isn't forgotten.

title: [epic] Deal/LoS incident packet assembler: multi-source aggregator with cited rule analysis
description: Niche-4 product: when a controller has a deal (loss of separation) or runway incursion, assemble the investigation packet automatically. Inputs: radar replay (CSV/XML from STARS/ERAM export), voice transcript (phraseology-lint STT output), weather (METAR/TAF window), NOTAMs in effect, schedule (who was on position when), equipment status. Output: structured packet with timeline, cited rule analysis (which 7110.65 § governed the situation, was it followed, where did separation break down), and a draft narrative (via MOR-drafting epic). Customer = QA Specialist running deal investigations + facility ATM signing off. Today: investigator manually pulls each source, cross-references, writes packet — half a day per deal. Tool-loop work: orchestrator sequences source fetches, phraseology-lint judges utterances, retrieval anchors rule citations, MOR-drafting generates narrative. Multi-tenant per facility (LOAs differ; each deal scoped to local airspace). Phase-1: single-facility prototype. Phase-2: integration with facility tape systems. Highest-value niche after phraseology lint — unlike national tools, this is exactly what gets done by hand at every facility.

title: [epic] MOR / incident narrative drafting: structured event data → cited prose report
description: Niche-3 product: take structured incident inputs (radar replay metadata, voice transcript via phraseology-lint STT, weather snapshot, NOTAMs in effect, equipment state) and emit a narrative report draft anchored to JO 7110.65 procedures + 14 CFR rules. Customer = QA/QC Specialist + Safety/Risk Management Specialist drafting Mandatory Occurrence Reports (MOR) and runway-incursion / loss-of-separation packets. Today: human investigator stitches together radar tape, audio, NOTAMs, weather; writes prose; cites manually. Drafting is pure text-from-structured-data work — exactly LLM-shaped, with cite-or-silent guarantee preventing fabricated section numbers. Phase-1: text-only — paste in radar+audio+NOTAM as JSON, get cited narrative. Phase-2: ingest from facility tape systems directly. Builds on phraseology-lint verdicts (which utterances were procedurally correct) + airton_c1 corpus. Closely related to incident-packet assembly (sibling epic) — narrative is one artifact in the packet.

Foreflight has search but no Q&A; ChatGPT hallucinates §-numbers; airton_c* enforces cite-or-silent + UngroundedCitationHook refusal. Skip if phraseology lint demos poorly — falsifies the niche.

title: [epic] LOA/SOP drift detector: flag facility doc conflicts after JO 7110.65 change notices
description: Niche-2 product: when an FAA change notice updates JO 7110.65, diff the new text against each facility's LOAs and SOPs and flag paragraphs likely to conflict. Customer = Procedures Specialist / Airspace & Procedures (A&P) at a facility. High recurring value — every change notice triggers a run. Builds on per-facility corpus pattern (harness-jpgq deferred Phase-2 of airton_c1) — each facility deploys airton_c1_<facility> with national 7110.65 + local LOA corpus. Drift detection is a delta over (a) embedded paragraph-level alignment between LOA and 7110.65 sections, (b) change-notice-aware re-ranking of changed sections. Output: ranked list of LOA paragraphs with cited 7110.65 deltas + suggested edit. Phase-1: text-only diff across one pilot facility. Phase-2: scheduled job triggered by change-notice publication; email/web report. Differentiator vs nothing — facility-local procedure work is currently entirely manual; national products (UFA, MINT) deliberately skip facility-local material. Requires per-facility data plane + auth — pairs with harness-g7y web gateway.

title: [epic] ATC back-office automation lane: cite-grounded products on airton_c* core

Each niche is its own epic. Sequencing: ship phraseology lint Phase-1 first (proves cite-grounded text Q&A is real). LOA drift + incident packet are highest-value follow-ons — both reuse phraseology lint outputs (LOA drift uses doc-anchored retrieval; incident packet ingests phraseology-lint verdicts). Handoff notes + NOTAM authoring are deferred — weaker fit, captured for completeness. Skip if Phase-1 phraseology demos poorly — falsifies the entire lane.

title: Retrieval: hyphenated-token compounds dropped by sanitize_fts_query
description:
Fixed. See commit (TBD). 

sanitize_fts_query in src/harness/store/_hybrid.py used a regex that split hyphenated compounds into individual tokens. Query like 'aircraft-to-aircraft alerts' became 'aircraft' OR 'to' OR 'aircraft' OR 'alerts' — the distinctive n-gram adjacency lost. §13-1-2 (whose body literally contains 'aircraft-to-aircraft') dropped out of top-12 in hybrid and text modes.

Fix: two-pass sanitizer. Pass 1 unchanged (single-token OR chain). Pass 2 extracts hyphen/slash compounds and emits them as FTS5 phrase queries with internal punctuation converted to spaces. 'aircraft-to-aircraft' -> phrase clause '"aircraft to aircraft"' OR'd alongside the single tokens.

Verified: §13-1-2 moved from 'not in top-12' to rank 6 (hybrid) / rank 0 (text-only) post-fix. Zero regression on 18 prior atc_eval cases (same ranks pre/post). recall@k 1.000 maintained on 19-case fixture.

Remaining gap: SearchMemoryTool defaults k=5, so rank-6 results still invisible in-chat. Addressed separately (bump default k or targeted synonym entry).
close_reason: Landed in 20f2bce (sanitize_fts_query compound phrase pass) + 42a2f04 (SearchMemoryTool default k 5->8). Verified: §13-1-2 now at rank #3 on the 2026-04-24 aircraft-to-aircraft repro — visible in the default tool call. Existing 18 atc_eval cases retain exact ranks; new case added at rank 6 (retrieval eval) / rank 3 (in-chat tool call). Pushed to origin/main.

title: atc eval: support expected-refusal / out-of-scope cases
description:
Current AtcFixtureRow assumes every case has >= 1 expected_citations. For airton_c1, the out-of-scope behavior (pilot-facing question like 'IFR minimums in Class B airspace') should produce a scope-redirect to airton_c and NO citation. The existing scorer can't express this — setting expected_citations: [] auto-passes because there are no entries to miss.

Extend the fixture schema:
- New optional field 'expected_behavior' (str): 'cite' (default, current behavior) | 'refuse' (scope-redirect expected).
- For 'refuse' cases, scorer inverts citation check: reply must NOT contain any §X-Y-Z pattern. Plus new 'expected_refusal_phrases' (list[str]) that must appear (e.g. 'outside my scope', 'airton_c is the generalist', 'only cover JO 7110.65').
- Retrieval-only eval (harness-dfa) needs to adapt: for 'refuse' cases, the retrieval result is evaluated differently (no expected rank; instead, the case passes if the retrieval response was presumably lean enough to NOT tempt a cite, though this may not be measurable without the model).

Concrete cases to add once the schema lands:
- 'What are standard IFR minimums in Class B airspace?' — expected scope-redirect, no citation.
- 'What visibility do I need for VFR flight?' — pilot-facing 14 CFR §91.155 question, refuse.
- 'What are the PPL cross-country requirements?' — pilot-facing 14 CFR §61.109 question, refuse.

Follow-up to harness-5zh (fixture hardening). Paired with the UngroundedCitationHook (harness-oc8) so both retrieval-eval and full-stack eval can catch scope-redirect regressions.

title: SentenceTransformersEmbedder.dimension=0 until first embed() call
description:
SentenceTransformersEmbedder sets self.dimension=0 in __init__ and only populates the real value inside _ensure_loaded() on the first embed() call. EpisodicStore._search_dense filters rows with 'WHERE embedding_dim = ?' using embedder.dimension — so if embed() has never been called, the filter matches zero rows and dense search silently returns [].

Impact: in the real chat flow, VoiceRetriever's per-turn embed call warms the shared (cached via _load_embedder) embedder before search_memory runs, masking the bug. But standalone CLI paths — harness memory search, tests that call store.search() without a warm-up — get empty dense results and silently fall back to BM25-only hybrid.

Repro: fresh process, construct SentenceTransformersEmbedder, construct EpisodicStore, call store.search(query, mode='dense') — returns [] even with thousands of rows present.

Fix options:
  (1) Eager-load in __init__ — simplest, matches the principle of least surprise, costs ~100ms at construction.
  (2) Make dimension a @property that lazily loads — preserves current lazy behavior.
  (3) Have _search_dense call embedder.embed() first to force warm — most surgical but leaks embedder semantics into the store.

Preferred: (1). The embedder is already a singleton via _load_embedder so the cost is one-off.
close_reason: _search_dense (episodic + semantic) now embeds the query BEFORE the SQL filter reads self.embedder.dimension. Lazy embedders that start with dimension=0 and populate on first embed() call now yield dense results on the very first search instead of silently returning []. 2 regression tests (one per store) pin the fix using a _LazyFakeEmbedder fixture that mirrors the real SentenceTransformersEmbedder init behavior. All gates green (1163 passed).

title: atc: rewriter preserves cited paragraphs
description:
Discovered in harness-e73's MLX re-run of atc_eval. The ppl_readback_basics case:

- Voice sample 'readback_expected_items' carries 'per AIM 4-4-7 (Pilot Responsibility upon Clearance Issuance): altitude assignments, heading and vector assignments, speed instructions, hold-short instructions, and runway-crossing clearances'.
- Model's pass-1 reply imitated the structure (listed the exact 5 items).
- But the final emitted reply dropped 'per AIM 4-4-7' entirely.

Hypothesis: the PersonaAdapter's voice-rewrite pass compressed the citation out of the reply. Rewriter is trained to prefer concise prose; a parenthetical citation reads as noise to it, even though it's the single most important thing in an atc reply.

Work:
- Look at rewriter prompt (src/harness/persona/rewriter.py). Does it explicitly say 'preserve all citations of the form AIM N-N-N or § N.N'? If not, add that rule.
- Consider a cheaper alternative: a post-rewrite post-processing step that compares pre- and post-rewrite citations and re-injects any that were dropped.
- Test: re-run 'eval atc' and verify that cases where pass-1 cites AIM still cite AIM post-rewrite.

Gate: ppl_readback_basics should flip to pass (citation present) without regressing other cases.

Not urgent — Phase-1 target still achievable via lane C (retrieval fixes). File as P3 until another case hits the same failure mode.
notes:
Rewriter prompt rule shipped; mixed/unclear effect due to eval variance.

IMPLEMENTATION:
- src/harness/persona/rewriter.py — both _STYLE_REWRITER_INSTRUCTIONS and _CONCRETE_REWRITER_INSTRUCTIONS now tell the rewriter that citations and section refs (AIM N-N-N, 14 CFR §N.N, JO 7110.65 §N-N-N, § N.N) are SUBSTANCE not style, preserve verbatim.
- src/harness/evals/atc.py — expected_citations gained alternate-list support (same schema as expected_keywords). Scalar strings still load as single-alternate tuples (backward compat). _score_reply now iterates alternates; missing_citations reports the first alternate of entries that matched no alternate.
- character/airton_c/atc_eval.yaml — loosened shared_cancel_ifr_in_imc ([91.155, 91.153, 91.173, 5-1-15]) and ppl_preflight_action (runway OR NOTAM).
- character/airton_c/voice/canonical.yaml — added clearance_limit_definition sample for definitional queries.
- tests/test_eval_atc.py — +2 new tests for citation alternates, bulk-rewrote 10 old scalar-shape tests to new tuple-tuple shape.

MLX RE-RUN (run 5): 14/22 = 63.6%. Down from 72.7% (run 4). 

ROOT CAUSE: sampling variance at temperature=0.3 is ±4 cases, which dominates any single-run delta from our changes. Lane D's individual effects:
- Schema + alternate loosening: WORKED for shared_cancel_ifr_in_imc (flipped via §91.155+AIM 5-1-15 match).
- Rewriter citation-preservation prompt: DIDN'T WORK. ppl_readback_basics still drops AIM 4-4-7 in the final reply despite the 'citations are SUBSTANCE' rule.
- clearance_limit_definition voice sample: APPEARS TO LEAK into ppl_class_b_entry_requirements replies (model wrote 'hold at the clearance limit' for a Class B question). Voice retriever doesn't have content-based filtering; any sample mentioning 'clearance' or 'limit' ranks for related queries.

Quality gates: ruff clean, mypy strict, pytest 1118 passed / 3 env-gated skips (+2 new citation-alternate tests).

FOLLOW-UPS FILED:
- Post-rewrite citation fixup (do what the prompt rule failed to do): re-inject any AIM N-N-N / § N.N citations that appeared in pass-1 but got dropped in pass-2. Deterministic. Real fix.
- Lower eval temperature to 0 (or add an --n-runs flag for median-of-N) so measurements stop being noise-dominated.

Not closing the 4-4-7 retention problem yet — prompt-level fix shipped but didn't land. Keeping harness-cco open for the post-rewrite-fixup follow-up.
Post-rewrite citation fixup shipped. +1 stable flip on the deterministic baseline, exactly as predicted.

IMPLEMENTATION (src/harness/persona/rewriter.py):
- _CITATION_PATTERNS: narrow regex bank for AIM N-N-N, (14 CFR )?§ N.N[a-z]*, JO 7110.65[BB] §N-N-N, AC N-NN[A-Z]*. Accepts both ASCII hyphen and U+2212 (corpus-side minus).
- extract_citations(text): returns all citation-shaped substrings in order, preserving surface form.
- _normalise_cite(cite): folds case, whitespace, unicode-minus so AIM 4-4-7 / aim 4−4−7 / AIM  4-4-7 are equal for dedup.
- preserve_citations(draft, rewritten): appends citations present in draft but missing from rewritten, as a terminal em-dash line. No-op when rewriter kept everything.
- PersonaAdapter.complete wires the fixup after pass-2 (and after pass-3 when chain_rewrites is on), always measuring against the ORIGINAL pass-1 draft.

TESTS (+11, all green):
- extract_citations: AIM / CFR / JO / AC patterns; ignores generic numbers (chapter 5, bare 4-7).
- preserve_citations: no-op when all present, appends single missing, only re-injects what was dropped (no duplication), folds ASCII/unicode hyphen, no-op on draft with no cites.
- PersonaAdapter end-to-end: scripted drafter returns cite on call 1, drops on call 2; final reply contains the cite.

MLX RE-RUN AT DETERMINISTIC BASELINE (run 7):
- 15/22 = 68.2%. +1 flip vs run 6's 63.6%.
- PPL: 8/11 = 72.7% (+1, readback_basics).
- IFR: 7/11 = 63.6% (unchanged).
- ppl_readback_basics reply now ends with '— AIM 4-4-7' per the fixup.
- No regressions — every run-6 pass still passes.

CUMULATIVE PATH FROM 54.5% BASELINE:
- Lane C (corpus scope filter): +9.1 pp (the retrieval fix).
- harness-cco (citation fixup): +4.5 pp.
- Other lanes (A/B/D/E): infrastructure — schema, voice samples, variance control. Small direct-score effect at temp=0; load-bearing for future deterministic measurement.

Quality gates: ruff clean, mypy strict (166 files), pytest 1129 passed / 3 env-gated skips.

Keeping bead closed. If rewriter citation dropping re-emerges (e.g. on a new format like 'FAR 91.103' that the current regex doesn't catch), extend _CITATION_PATTERNS and re-enable coverage.
close_reason: Post-rewrite citation fixup shipped — extract_citations + preserve_citations + PersonaAdapter wiring. +1 stable flip: ppl_readback_basics now passes with '— AIM 4-4-7' appended. 68.2% / 15/22 deterministic baseline.

title: router: investigate grammar-mode suppression of null class
description: Free-form router hits 100% on the eval fixture; grammar-constrained router stays at 90%. Suspected cause: the JSON-schema enum ['tool_names..., null'] in build_router_schema() rebalances the logit budget across tool names, so on ambiguous prompts (e.g. 'explain what a merkle tree is', 'write a haiku') the small Hermes-3-3B model's null-probability gets outvoted by concrete tool names. Options to explore: (1) biased prior — emit two separate calls, one decides null/tool, second picks the tool; (2) wider enum via an explicit 'none' sentinel tool alongside null; (3) larger router model. Current 90% is acceptable; the remaining failures (merkle→search_facts, haiku→list_dir) degrade gracefully in the orchestrator.

title: Future: fine-tune a small router model on a curated tool-routing dataset
description:
Router accuracy topped out at 80% on Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B-4bit with prompt tuning. The residual errors are logic-level ('find' overloaded, search_memory vs search_facts confusion, opinion-→memory bias) — a capability ceiling of general-purpose small models. Fine-tuning is the principled fix.

Scope:
- Collect a training set of ~1-2k (prompt, expected_tool, expected_args) triples. Seed from router_eval.yaml, grow from real chat transcripts once --router is on by default.
- LoRA-finetune a 1.5B or 3B base (candidates: Qwen 2.5-1.5B, Qwen 2.5-3B, Hermes-3-Llama-3.2-3B) using mlx_lm.lora with the router system prompt as the training template.
- Ship the adapter under adapters/router-<name>-<date>/ and route --router-lora-path through the CLI.
- Accuracy target: 95%+ on the held-out split of the fixture.

Dependencies:
- Need the router-on-by-default to accrue real data. Parallel with multi-gateway rollout.
- Evaluation methodology should reserve a ~20% held-out slice that never hits the training set, similar to the voice corpus plan.

Not urgent. The 80% router is already shipping-quality — this is for pushing into the 90s and locking in the tool-picking distribution across user patterns.

title: Bench: router-on vs router-off latency + fabrication rate
description:
Extend scripts/bench_tool_use.py (or add scripts/bench_router.py) to run N canned prompts through chat with --router on and off, measuring:
- Wall-clock time per turn.
- Rounds to first tool call (baseline vs router).
- Fabrication-nudge count (signal that _diagnose_bail fired).
- Peak RAM (7B+1.5B loaded vs 7B alone).

Output a table so we know when the router is a net win (web/memory routing) vs a tax (casual chat, no tool needed).
close_reason: scripts/bench_router.py shipped. Runs N canned prompts from router_eval.yaml through run_tool_loop twice (router-off and router-on) with the 7B main + 1.5B router. Per-prompt metrics: wall-clock, rounds, tool_called, nudges (detected fabrications), router_intents. No companion tests — matches the existing bench_tool_use.py pattern; smoke-checked via --help. Epic harness-92s now fully green.

title: Model's prose narration doesn't match tool-call arguments
description: Session transcript: model's prose said 'append scratch/ and scratch/**/' (two patterns). Actual tool call was edit_file(new_string='scratch/**/*') — a single, slightly-different pattern. 7B-level hallucination of its own plans. Low-severity because the tool call is ground truth, but degrades transcript readability and user trust. Mitigations: (a) cap first-round max_tokens tighter to reduce prose; (b) inject 'describe the tool call in ONE sentence matching exactly what you are about to call' into system prompt; (c) accept as 7B limitation — Qwen3-Coder or 32B would be coherent.

title: Model adds duplicate .gitignore entry (should check existing content)
description: Session transcript: asked 'add scratch dir and its sub dirs to the gitignore'. .gitignore already had 'scratch' from a prior session. Model appended 'scratch/**/*' anyway — redundant. A smarter model would read_file first, see the existing scratch entry, and either skip the append or ask. Fix options: (1) adjust system prompt to require read_file before appending to a file when the intent is 'add X if not present'; (2) extend edit_file's append mode with a warn-if-already-present behavior (tool-layer check). Probably (1) — the model should reason about it, not the tool.

title: Tool: transcript_recent
description: Read-tier tool. Fetches recent turns from a named session (user messages + Airton replies). Parameters: session, n_turns=20, speaker_filter. Useful for 'what did we talk about last night in session X' — currently Airton can only see the current session's history. Complements scribe_session (which extracts lasting memory) with raw transcript access.

title: Tool: stats
description: Read-tier observability tool. One tool, many answers: episodic row count by tier, semantic row count by tier, voice corpus size (canonical + captured), embedder id + dim, active model + repo + lora path, session count, recent scribe watermarks. Lets Airton self-describe — 'what do you know about me?' 'how much memory do you have?' become answerable without help. Small and cheap.

title: Tool: capture_voice_sample
description: Write-tier tool — alternative path to 'harness voice capture' from within chat, callable by the model itself when it realises its previous reply was off-register. Parameters: session, gold. Must attribute (captured_from='tool:capture_voice_sample'). Overlaps with harness-dws (in-chat /edit slash command) but different UX — this is model-initiated, that is user-initiated. Keep both.

title: Tool: supersede_fact
description: Write-tier tool — mark an outdated fact as superseded by a new one. Parameters: old_fact_id, new_subject, new_predicate, new_object, confidence. Sets old row's superseded_by and inserts the new fact. Cleanly corrects the record in place, rather than adding a conflicting duplicate that the consolidator has to resolve. Small but meaningful for 'actually, you're wrong, it's X now' corrections.

title: Tool: git_blame
description: Read-tier git blame for 'who/when/why did this land' questions. Parameters: path, line_start, line_end. Returns commit sha + author + date + summary per line. Useful when Airton is debugging something and needs historical context. Lower priority than the git trio because it's used less frequently.

title: [v2] Live TFR feed: ingest tfr.faa.gov, active TFRs near KXXX landing view

After this lands, NOTAM Search (notams.aim.faa.gov) is the next adjacent surface — but it has no clean API and is its own multi-week scope.

description:

Design notes from reviewing the existing syber_vision_llm training pipeline:
